questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An attorney filed a class action in federal court on behalf of thousands of individuals against a cell phone company that is incorporated and has its principal place of business in State C. The two named plaintiffs are citizens of State A and State B, respectively, and the unnamed plaintiffs reside in every other state. The complaint alleges that the company violated a law enacted by states nationwide by overcharging its customers $3.50 per month for the past 20 months. The damages on behalf of the entire class are alleged to be $10 million.
The cell phone company moved to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Will the federal court likely grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over class actions.
choices.B: No, because the amount in controversy is sufficient in the aggregate.
choices.C: Yes, because at least one of the unnamed plaintiffs is not diverse from the company.
choices.D: Yes, because the amount in controversy is insufficient individually.

questions.explanation:
Subject-matter jurisdiction in class actions
Type Requirements
Federal question • Class action arises under U.S. Constitution, treaty, or federal law
Diversity • Amount in controversy for any named plaintiff's claim exceeds $75,000* and
• named opposing parties are citizens of different states
Class Action
Fairness Act		 • Class contains ≥ 100 members
• at least one class member & one defendant are diverse and
• amount in controversy for aggregated claims exceeds $5 million

*A federal court can acquire subject-matter jurisdiction over class members' claims that do not exceed $75,000 through supplemental jurisdiction.

A federal district court's subject-matter jurisdiction over a class action, like any other lawsuit, can arise from either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – the class action arises from the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not state law, as seen here) or
  • diversity jurisdiction – the named opposing parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy for any named plaintiff's claim exceeds $75,000.

Here, no single plaintiff can individually satisfy the amount-in-controversy requirement because the complaint alleges that the cell phone company overcharged each plaintiff only $70 ($3.50 × 20 months). And individual claims generally cannot be aggregated (ie, added together) unless an alternate basis of subject-matter jurisdiction over the class action exists. The Class Action Fairness Act (CAFA) provides such a basis when:

  • the class contains at least 100 members
  • any class member is diverse from at least one defendant (ie, minimal diversity) and
  • the amount in controversy exceeds $5 million when the members' claims are aggregated.

Here, the class contains over 100 members. And since unnamed plaintiffs live in each state, at least one member of that class is diverse from the defendant cell phone company (Choice C). Furthermore, the amount in controversy—based on the class members' aggregated damages—is $10 million. Therefore, the CAFA does apply, and the court will likely deny the company's motion to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction (Choice D).

(Choice A) Federal courts do not have exclusive jurisdiction over class actions. The reason is that state and federal courts have concurrent jurisdiction over claims arising from state or federal law unless the Constitution or Congress expressly states otherwise (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The Class Action Fairness Act gives a federal court an alternative basis for subject-matter jurisdiction over a class action when (1) the class contains 100 members, (2) at least one class member is diverse from at least one defendant, and (3) the amount in controversy of the aggregated claims exceeds $5 million.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1331 (federal-question jurisdiction).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction and the Class Action Fairness Act).
questions.zh-question:
一名律师代表数千名个人，在联邦法院对一家手机公司提起集体诉讼，该公司在 C 州注册成立且其主要营业地也在 C 州。两名具名原告分别是 A 州和 B 州的公民，而未具名原告则居住在所有其他州。诉状指控，该公司违反了全国各州颁布的一项法律，在过去 20 个月里，每月向其客户多收取 3.50 美元。据称，整个集体的损害赔偿总额为 1000 万美元。

该手机公司以缺乏标的物管辖权为由，请求驳回起诉。

联邦法院是否可能批准该请求？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为联邦法院对集体诉讼拥有专属管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为总争议金额已足够。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为至少有一名未具名原告与该公司不具有多样性。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为个别原告的争议金额不足。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Subject-matter jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：集体诉讼（class action）能不能靠CAFA进联邦法院，而不是每个原告自己都要凑满 $75,000。

三秒认题路径：

多人集体诉讼 → 先看 CAFA → 100人以上 → 最低多元 → 争议额超500万

核心法律规则

联邦管辖（subject-matter jurisdiction）在集体诉讼里，除了 federal-question jurisdiction 和普通 diversity jurisdiction，还可以走 Class Action Fairness Act（CAFA）。考场意思：你不用硬把每个原告都塞进“单独超过 $75,000”这个框里。

CAFA 看三件事：class 至少 100 人、至少一名集体成员和一名被告是不同州公民、聚合后的争议额超过 $5 million。考场意思：只要这三关过了，联邦法院通常就有管辖权。

核心判例： 本题用的是 CAFA 规则，不是靠每个原告单独满足传统多元管辖；因此“人数够、最小多元、总额够”就能把案子留在联邦法院。

思维导图

1. 先看普通多元？
名义原告与公司不同州没问题，但每名原告个人损失只有 $70，凑不够传统 $75,000。
2. 再看 CAFA 人数
题干说是 thousands of individuals，明显超过 100 人。
3. 最低多元
两名命名原告来自 A / B 州，被告在 C 州，至少一名集体成员与被告不同州。
4. 聚合争议额
全体损失主张为 $10 million，直接超过 $5 million。
5. 卡死结论
CAFA 三要件齐，motion to dismiss 会被驳回；答案选 No。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：每个原告单独只有 $70，所以金额不够，法院应该直接没有管辖权。

但考试真正问的是：class action 能不能靠 CAFA 把成员的请求聚合起来看，答案是可以。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「每个个人原告单独拿了多少钱」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 thousands of individuals 且总额 $10 million，正好满足 CAFA 的人数、最低多元和聚合金额要求，所以联邦法院不会因管辖权不足而驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 exclusive jurisdiction 当成默认规则了。

❌ 事实误判 | 最低多元偷换

✕ C: 题干已给出 minimal diversity，你不能只盯着“有人同州”乱扣帽子。

❌ 法律适用 | 个人金额误套

✕ D: 这是拿单个原告的 individual 金额去卡集体诉讼。

这题建议用什么方法？

先别纠结每人赔多少，直接按“CAFA 三要件”快速筛一遍。

考场速记

记忆口诀：CAFA 三件套——100人以上、最低多元、聚合超500万。考试一看集体诉讼，先想“能不能合并算总账”，别被单个原告的小额损失带跑。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
In a state court of general jurisdiction in State A, a debtor, who was a resident of State A, brought suit against a lender, who was a noncitizen with permanent residency status in State B, for violation of the federal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. The lender waived personal jurisdiction. Under state procedural rules, venue was proper in the state court. The lender timely removed the action to the federal court for the Northern District of State A, which was the district in which the state court sat. The lender then timely moved to dismiss the action for improper venue, arguing that, had the action initially been brought in federal court, the federal court for the Northern District of State A would not have had proper venue over this action.
How should the court rule on this motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the state court sits in the federal Northern District of State A.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because venue was proper in the state court under state procedural rules before the action was removed.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the federal court for the Northern District of State A would not have had proper venue over this action had it initially been brought in federal court.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the lender is deemed to reside in the judicial district where the lender is domiciled.

questions.explanation:
Special rules for where venue is proper
Removal
  • Federal district where state action was pending
Foreign resident
  • Any judicial district
Federal official sued in official capacity
  • Where defendant resides
  • Where substantial events occurred or property is located
  • Where plaintiff resides if no real property is involved in suit
Foreign government
  • Where substantial events occurred or property is located
  • In federal district court of Washington, D.C.
Multiparty, multiforum litigation
  • Where defendant resides
  • Where substantial part of accident occurred
Federal Tort Claims Act
  • Where plaintiff resides
  • Where act/omission occurred

Typically, the general venue rules govern whether venue is proper. However, venue can also be established through special venue rules in certain situations, including when a suit is removed from state court to federal court. In that situation, venue is proper in the federal district encompassing the state court from which the suit was removed—even if venue would otherwise be improper. This is because the defendant has consented to venue by removing the suit to that federal district.

Here, the debtor initially sued the lender in a state court in State A. The lender then timely removed the action from that state court to the federal court for the Northern District of State A. And since the state court sits in the federal Northern District of State A (i.e., the federal district encompassing the state court), venue is proper there. Therefore, the court should deny the lender's motion to dismiss for improper venue.

(Choice B) The federal rules regarding proper venue when a case is removed do not turn on whether venue was proper in the state court from which the case was removed.

(Choice C) In a removed action, venue is proper in the federal court in the district where the action was pending—regardless of whether venue would have been proper had the action initially been brought in that district.

(Choice D) A noncitizen lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the U.S. (e.g., the lender) is deemed to reside in the judicial district where that person is domiciled—here, a federal district in State B. But here, venue is proper in the Northern District of State A because the case was removed from a state court in that district.

📌 Educational Objective

When a lawsuit is removed from state court to federal court, venue is proper in the federal district encompassing the state court from which the suit was removed—even if venue would otherwise be improper.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. 1441(a) (providing that venue is proper in the federal district to which a state court action is removed if the federal district encompasses the state court where the action was initially brought).
questions.zh-question: 在A州的一家普通管辖权州法院中，一名作为A州居民的债务人起诉了一名在B州拥有永久居民身份的非美国公民债权人，指控其违反了联邦《公平债务催收作业法》（Fair Debt Collection Practices Act）。该债权人放弃了对人管辖权（personal jurisdiction）异议。根据州诉讼规则，该州法院的管辖地（venue）是适当的。债权人及时将该诉讼移送（removed）至A州北区联邦地区法院（该州法院位于该联邦司法区内）。随后，债权人及时提出动议，以管辖地不当（improper venue）为由请求驳回诉讼，理由是：如果该诉讼最初是在联邦法院提起，A州北区联邦地区法院对本案将不具有适当的管辖地。法院应如何对该动议做出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 否决该动议，因为该州法院位于A州北区联邦司法区内。
zh-choices.B: 否决该动议，因为在诉讼被移送之前，根据州诉讼规则，该州法院的管辖地是适当的。
zh-choices.C: 准予该动议，因为如果该诉讼最初是在联邦法院提起，A州北区联邦地区法院对本案将不具有适当的管辖地。
zh-choices.D: 准予该动议，因为债权人被视为居住在其住所地（domicile）所在的司法管辖区。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Venue

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：移送案件（removed action）里，联邦法院的 venue 怎么算——看的是州法院所在的联邦司法区，不看“如果一开始就起诉在联邦法院会不会合适”。

三秒认题路径：

州诉 → 移送 → 看1441 → 州院在哪区 → venue成立

核心法律规则

移送（removal）后，venue 的考场意思很简单：看州法院被移到哪个联邦司法区，只要那个联邦区包住原来的州法院，venue 就 proper。

这里不要被“如果原告一开始就起诉在联邦法院会不会 improper”带跑；那是另一套一般 venue 规则，不是移送案件的 special rule。

所以这题只要抓住：州案是从 State A 的州法院移到 Northern District of State A，venue 就成立。

核心判例/法条： 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a)——州法院案件移送到“包住原州法院”的联邦区时，venue 直接成立。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决（final judgment）吗？
不是
再看：有没有法定中间上诉？
本题没有 § 1292 类特殊上诉入口
继续看
这题不是上诉题，但同样是 移送（removal） 的 venue 题：联邦 venue 看移送落点。
关键信号
州法院在 State A → 移到 Northern District of State A → venue 直接 proper
排除误区
不要问“联邦一般 venue 规则是否本来就满足”——移送规则已经单独解决。
答案落点
A：拒绝驳回，因为州法院坐落在该联邦区内。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然原告如果一开始就起诉在联邦法院，这里 venue 可能不合适，那就该直接驳回。

但考试真正问的是：这是移送案件，不是初始起诉案件。 移送以后，venue 的关键是原州法院所在的联邦司法区。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 state court sat in the Northern District of State A，移送后 venue 就落在这个联邦区，所以不能因 venue 不当而驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 州规套用

✕ B: 把 state procedural rules 当成移送后的联邦 venue 标准了。

❌ 法律适用 | 初始起诉误判

✕ C: 拿“如果一开始起诉”来卡题，但移送案件不看这一步。

❌ 事实误判 | 居所替换

✕ D: 盯着 domiciled 乱算住址，却忽略了移送规则直接定 venue。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先认出移送，再直接套 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a) 的特殊 venue 规则。

考场速记

一句话记忆： 移送（removal）后先别翻一般 venue 表，先看原州法院在哪个联邦区；包住原州法院的那个区，就是 proper venue。

口诀：“州案移联邦，先找原州法院；法院落哪区，venue 就在哪。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An accounting firm incorporated and headquartered in State A advertised its estate-planning services. An attorney in State A saw the firm's advertisement and wrote a newspaper editorial claiming that the firm violated State A's statute on the unauthorized practice of law by not employing licensed attorneys. After the editorial was published, demand for the firm's estate-planning services significantly declined. The firm then sued the attorney for defamation in a State A federal court to recover $150,000.
In his answer, the attorney asserted that the editorial contained truthful statements protected by the free speech clause of the First Amendment. The attorney also asserted a $100,000 counterclaim to recover damages suffered as a result of the firm's suit. The attorney did not object to venue or jurisdiction. After the pleadings were filed and served, the court dismissed the case for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. The firm appealed.
Is the appellate court likely to reverse the dismissal?

choices.A: No, because the final-judgment rule prevents the appellate court from considering the appeal.
choices.B: No, because the firm failed to establish subject-matter jurisdiction.
choices.C: Yes, because the attorney did not object to the court's jurisdiction.
choices.D: Yes, because the suit involves a federal question.

questions.explanation:
Well-pleaded complaint rule
(for federal-question jurisdiction)
Federal issue
= element of plaintiff's claim

I. Basis for Jurisdiction

  1. Plaintiff asserts that defendant committed trademark infringement in violation of the Lanham Act, 15 U.S.C. § 114.
Federal issue
≠ anticipated defense, counterclaim, answer

I. Affirmative Defense

  1. Defendant asserts that the state law violates the 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution.

II. Counterclaim

  1. Defendant asserts that plaintiff engaged in discriminatory practices in violation of 42 U.S.C § 2000(e)-2.

Subject-matter jurisdiction is a federal court's authority to hear the merits of a particular case or controversy. This is a pure legal issue that an appellate court reviews de novo, giving no deference to the legal conclusions made by the lower court. This jurisdictional requirement can be established through:

  • diversity jurisdiction – when the amount in controversy in the plaintiff's complaint exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states (not seen here) or
  • federal-question jurisdiction – when the plaintiff asserts a claim that arises under the Constitution, a federal law, or a federal treaty.

Federal-question jurisdiction must be established on the face of the plaintiff's well-pleaded complaint—as opposed to the defendant's answer or counterclaim.* This means that the complaint must show that the federal issue is a necessary element of the plaintiff's cause of action. If the asserted federal issue is frivolous or later abandoned, then federal-question jurisdiction ceases to exist.

Here, the firm sued the attorney for defamation, a state-law claim. The attorney defended on the ground that this editorial contained truthful statements protected by the First Amendment. Since this federal issue arose in the attorney's answer—not the firm's complaint—the court lacks federal-question jurisdiction (Choice D). Therefore, the appellate court is not likely to reverse the dismissal.

*Congress created an exception that authorizes federal-question jurisdiction when a defendant (1) asserts a counterclaim arising from a federal patent or copyright statute and (2) removes the case from state to federal court.

(Choice A) The final-judgment rule generally precludes federal appellate courts from hearing an appeal until the federal district court has entered a final judgment—i.e., a decision that fully resolves a dispute on the merits and leaves nothing for the court to do but enforce the judgment. A dismissal for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is a final judgment, so the appellate court here can consider the appeal.

(Choice B) Subject-matter jurisdiction cannot be waived or consented to, so it is immaterial that the attorney did not object to the court's jurisdiction. Instead, a court must dismiss a case on its own initiative (ie, sua sponte) if, at any time, it determines that it lacks subject-matter jurisdiction.

(Choice C) Here, the firm sued the attorney for defamation, a state-law claim. The attorney defended on the ground that this editorial contained truthful statements protected by the First Amendment. Since this federal issue arose in the attorney's answer—not the firm's complaint—the court lacks federal-question jurisdiction.

(Choice D) Therefore, the appellate court is not likely to reverse the dismissal.

📌 Educational Objective

Federal-question jurisdiction exists when a claim arising under the Constitution, a federal law, or a federal treaty appears on the face of the plaintiff's complaint. A federal issue raised in the defendant's answer or counterclaim does not establish federal-question jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1331 (federal-question jurisdiction).
  • Louisville & Nashville R.R. Co. v. Mottley, 211 U.S. 149, 152 (1908) (establishing the well-pleaded complaint rule).
  • Holmes Group, Inc. v. Vornado Air Circulation Sys., Inc., 535 U.S. 826, 831 (2002) (holding that a defendant's answer or counterclaim does not establish federal-question jurisdiction).

一家在A州注册并设立总部的会计师事务所，为其遗产规划服务做广告。A州的一名律师看到了该事务所的广告，并撰写了一篇报纸社论，声称该事务所因未雇佣执业律师而违反了A州关于未经授权执业的法规。社论发表后，市场对该事务所遗产规划服务的需求大幅下降。该事务所随后以诽谤为由，在A州的联邦法院起诉该律师，要求赔偿15万美元。

在其答辩中，该律师声称社论包含受《第一修正案》言论自由条款保护的真实陈述。该律师还提起了10万美元的反诉，要求赔偿因该事务所的诉讼而遭受的损失。该律师未对审判地或管辖权提出异议。在诉状提交并送达后，法院以缺乏标的物管辖权为由驳回了此案。该事务所提起了上诉。

上诉法院是否可能推翻该驳回裁定？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为法院在缺乏标的物管辖权时，有自由裁量权驳回案件。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该事务所未能确立标的物管辖权。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该律师未对法院的管辖权提出异议。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该诉讼涉及联邦问题。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Subject-matter jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦问题管辖（federal-question jurisdiction）必须写在原告的起诉状（complaint）里，不能靠被告答辩里的第一修正案抗辩来补。

三秒认题路径：

州法侵权 → 看起诉状 → 有无联邦要素 → 答辩不算 → 无管辖

核心法律规则

联邦问题管辖（federal-question jurisdiction）要看原告的善状起诉状（well-pleaded complaint），考场意思：联邦问题必须是原告诉求本身的必要要件。Affirmative defense、counterclaim（反诉）、answer（答辩）里冒出来的联邦问题，通常都不算。

所以这题里，原告告的是defamation（诽谤），这是州法请求；被告说“这篇社论受第一修正案保护”只是抗辩，考场意思：它不能把一个州法案子变成联邦案。

如果法院一开始就没有subject-matter jurisdiction（标的管辖权），法院可以主动发现并驳回；这和被告有没有反对无关。

核心判例： Louisville & Nashville R.R. Co. v. Mottley — 联邦问题必须出现在原告起诉状上，不能靠被告答辩或抗辩“塞进去”。

思维导图

先看：原告的起诉状里有没有联邦问题？
YES 原告请求本身就依赖联邦法/宪法/条约 → 可考虑联邦问题管辖。
NO 这题原告告的是defamation（州法侵权），联邦因素只出现在被告答辩里。
卡死点：answer 里的第一修正案抗辩不算管辖基础。
再看 被告的counterclaim（反诉）也不补管辖，除非是极少数法定例外。
结论 没有联邦问题管辖 → 驳回正确 → 上诉法院不太会推翻。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告提到了First Amendment，这不就是联邦宪法问题吗？

但考试真正问的是：这个联邦问题是不是原告起诉状里的必要要素。不是的话，就算写进answer（答辩），也救不回管辖。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里联邦因素只出现在被告答辩中的第一修正案抗辩，原告的诽谤诉讼本身还是州法案子，所以联邦问题管辖没建立起来。

❌ 法律适用 | 终局规则误判

✕ A: 把final-judgment rule当挡箭牌；这里真正问题是管辖，不是能不能上诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 管辖可放弃误判

✕ C: 以为没反对就能补出管辖，did not object 不会把缺失的标的管辖变出来。

❌ 事实误判 | 答辩联邦化误判

✕ D: 盯着federal question就选是，但联邦点不在起诉状里。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看原告起诉状，再判断联邦要素是不是构成诉因的一部分。

考场速记

记忆口诀：联邦问题看起诉状，不看答辩和反诉。看到州法请求里突然冒出联邦抗辩，先想 Mottley。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A custom car owner domiciled in State A agreed to drive across the country to State B to deliver a car to a buyer pursuant to the contract between the two parties. The buyer had agreed to purchase the car after seeing the owner's advertisement for buying and selling used, custom cars on a website that was accessible across the nation.
As the owner drove toward State B, he got into a car accident in State C. The driver of the other car was domiciled in State D and was vacationing in State C. The owner did not suffer any physical harm, but the other driver was taken to the nearest hospital to be treated for her injuries. After being released from the hospital, the driver returned home to State D, where she continues to receive treatment for her injuries.
Three months after the accident, the driver sued the owner in a federal district court in State D to recover $1 million for the personal injuries she suffered. After the owner was properly served with process in State A, he immediately moved to dismiss the suit for lack of personal jurisdiction.
State D has a long-arm statute that gives its courts personal jurisdiction to the full extent allowed under the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause.
How should the federal court rule on the owner's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because it is foreseeable that vacationers from State D will drive in State C.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the owner's website was accessible in State D.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the claim does not arise from and is not closely related to the owner's minimum contacts with State D.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the claim may only be brought in a court located in State C.

questions.explanation:
Personal jurisdiction
(court's authority over defendant)
Type Requirements
Service of
process		 • Serving process on defendant voluntarily in state where court is located (ie, forum state)
Consent • Express – contractual agreement (eg, forum-selection clause)
• Implied – engaging in specific activity that state has substantial interest in regulating (eg, driving on public roads)
• Waiver – untimely objection to personal jurisdiction
• Appearance – voluntarily appearing in court to litigate merits of case
Specific
(case-linked)		 • Plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to defendant's minimum contacts (ie, purposeful availment) with forum state AND
• Exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play & substantial justice
General
(all-purpose)		 • Defendant has continuous & systematic contacts with forum state so substantial that defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, defendant's domicile)

A court must have personal jurisdiction—ie, authority over the parties (or property) before the court—to hear a case. A federal court has the same personal jurisdiction as the courts of the state in which it is located (ie, the forum state). If a defendant has not consented to a court's personal jurisdiction or been served with process within the forum state, personal jurisdiction must be established through:

  • general jurisdiction – when the defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, where a defendant is domiciled) or
  • specific jurisdiction – when the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and the exercise of jurisdiction would comply with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

Here, the federal court in State D lacks general jurisdiction over the owner since he is domiciled in State A. The court also lacks specific jurisdiction because the driver's claim arises from and is closely related to the owner's minimum contacts with State C (where the accident occurred)—not State D (the forum state). Therefore, the court should grant the owner's motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) Whether it is foreseeable that drivers from other states (including State D) will drive in State C is irrelevant since personal jurisdiction turns on the defendant's contacts with the forum state—State D.

(Choice B) The driver's claim arises out of the car accident in State C—not the owner's nationwide, online advertisement that was accessible in State D.

(Choice C) Grant the motion, because the claim does not arise from and is not closely related to the owner's minimum contacts with State D.

(Choice D) A court in State C could have exercised specific jurisdiction over the claim since the accident occurred there. But a court in State A could also have exercised general jurisdiction since the owner is domiciled there.

📌 Educational Objective

Specific personal jurisdiction exists when (1) the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and (2) the exercise of jurisdiction would comply with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

📚 References
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the minimum contacts required for specific jurisdiction).
  • Goodyear Dunlop Tires Operations, S.A. v. Brown, 564 U.S. 915, 926–29 (2011) (discussing the continuous and systematic contacts required for general jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
一名居住在A州的定制车车主同意根据双方合同，驾车穿越全国前往B州，向一名买家交付一辆汽车。该买家是在一个全国范围内可访问的网站上看到车主发布的买卖二手定制车的广告后，同意购买此车的。

在车主驾车前往B州的途中，他在C州发生了一起车祸。另一辆车的司机居住在D州，当时正在C州度假。车主没有受到任何身体伤害，但另一名司机被送往最近的医院治疗其伤势。出院后，该司机返回其位于D州的家中，并继续因其伤势接受治疗。

事故发生三个月后，该司机在D州的联邦地区法院起诉了车主，要求赔偿其所受人身伤害的100万美元。车主在A州被合法送达诉讼文书后，他立即以缺乏对人管辖权为由，动议驳回该诉讼。

D州有一项长臂法，该法在宪法第十四修正案正当程序条款允许的最大范围内，授予其法院对人管辖权。

联邦法院应如何裁定车主提出的驳回动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为可以预见到来自D州的度假者会在C州驾车。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为车主的网站在D州可以访问。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为该诉求并非源于车主与D州的最低限度联系。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为该诉求只能在位于C州的法院提起。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告在论坛州没有足够的 最低联系（minimum contacts），所以 特定人身管辖权（specific personal jurisdiction） 不能成立。

三秒认题路径：

先看论坛州 → 再看联系点 → 先查一般管辖 → 再查特定管辖 → 不能上诉式硬留

核心法律规则

联邦法院的 人身管辖权（personal jurisdiction），和所在州法院一样，看的是论坛州能不能管到被告。被告如果没在论坛州被送达，也没同意管辖，就要看两条：一般管辖（general jurisdiction） 或 特定管辖（specific jurisdiction）。

一般管辖（general jurisdiction） 只看被告是不是“在家”——通常就是 住所地（domicile）；特定管辖（specific jurisdiction） 则要求本案请求和被告对 论坛州（forum state） 的联系有关联，不能只靠全国性广告或别州事故硬拉进来。

考试里记住：arises out of or relates to 说的是“这起诉讼和论坛州联系有没有直接勾上”，不是“被告有没有在全国范围内做过事”。

核心判例： Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Superior Court — 特定管辖要看诉请是否源于或密切相关于论坛州联系；Goodyear 则说明一般管辖要被告“在家”。

思维导图

先问：State D 能不能管这名被告？
NO 1 被告没在 State D 送达（service of process），也没 同意（consent）。
NO 2 再看 一般管辖（general jurisdiction）：被告 住所在 State A，不在 State D。
NO 3 再看 特定管辖（specific jurisdiction）：本案是 State C 的车祸，和 State D 没对上。
卡死点 State D 里的全国广告 + 以后会不会有人去 State C 驾车，都救不了“论坛州联系”
结论：State D 联邦法院应当 准许驳回（grant the motion to dismiss）。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告发了全国都能看的网页广告，而且原告又是 State D 住民，所以 State D 应该能管。

但考试真正问的是：这起伤害诉讼有没有 指向论坛州的最低联系；本题的事故发生在 State C，广告也不是把这起车祸“拉回” State D。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干关键点是事故发生在 State C，且被告在 State D 没有可供本案依附的 minimum contacts；因此 State D 既没有一般管辖，也没有特定管辖。

❌ 事实误判 | 旅行风险误读

✕ A: 把别人会在外州开车当成对 State D 的联系，错抓了对象。

❌ 概念混淆 | 网页联系误判

✕ B: 看到 accessible nationwide 就以为够了，但广告没和这起事故挂钩。

❌ 法律适用 | 诉讼地点偷换

✕ D: 把“哪里起诉都行”当成规则，实际上管辖看的是被告和论坛州，不是事故发生地想当然。

这题建议用什么方法？

先排一般管辖，再盯特定管辖的“本案是否和论坛州联系相关”这一刀。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先问“在家吗”，再问“这案子和论坛州有关吗”。General = at home；Specific = claim links to forum contacts。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A university student, a citizen of State A, believes that her university violated federal law when it eliminated funding for the women's varsity volleyball team. She has sued the university, a nonprofit corporation located and incorporated in State B, and the university's athletic director, a citizen of State B, in federal court in State B.
What is the best method of serving the defendants?

choices.A: Service as required by State B's rules of civil procedure.
choices.B: Service by a process server's leaving copies of the summons and complaint with secretaries in the respective offices of the athletic director and the university president.
choices.C: Service by emailing copies of the summons and complaint to the athletic director and the university president.
choices.D: Service by the student herself on the athletic director and the university president.

questions.explanation:
Methods of serving process in U.S.
Individual
  • Following state law where district court is located or where service is made
  • Personally serving defendant with summons & complaint
  • Leaving summons & complaint at defendant's dwelling with someone of suitable age & discretion who resides there
  • Delivering summons & complaint to defendant's authorized agent
Organization
  • Following state law where district court is located or where service is made
  • Delivering summons & complaint to officer, managing or general agent, or authorized agent & mailing those documents to defendant if required by statute

Due process prohibits a court from adjudicating a defendant's rights before the defendant has received proper notice of the plaintiff's complaint. A defendant receives proper notice when someone who is at least 18 years old and not a party to the suit serves the defendant with a summons and complaint. And under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 4, any defendant (an individual or organization) can be served for a federal suit by following the state law for serving process in the state where the court is located or where service is made.

Here, the student sued the university (organization) and its athletic director (individual) in federal court in State B. Since the defendants can be served under the civil procedure rules of State B (where the court is located), this is the best method of serving both defendants.

(Choice B) Individuals and organizations can be served by delivering a copy of the summons and complaint to an agent authorized to receive service on the defendant's behalf. But since there is no indication that the secretaries were authorized agents of either defendant, this is not the best method for serving the defendants.

(Choice C) Service of process by email is not expressly authorized under FRCP 4. Therefore, absent some indication that State B's rules allow this method of service, email is not the best method of serving the defendants.

(Choice D) The student herself cannot serve process because she is a party to the lawsuit. However, any nonparty who is at least 18 years old can serve process. If service was not waived and occurred within the U.S., the process server must typically file a proof of service affidavit.*

*Service in a foreign country can be proved (1) pursuant to an applicable treaty or convention, (2) by a receipt signed by the addressee, or (3) by other evidence that satisfies the court. However, failure to prove service in the U.S. or abroad does not affect the validity of the service.

📌 Educational Objective

Any defendant (individual or organization) can be served by (1) following the service-of-process laws of the state where the court is located or where service is made or (2) delivering a copy of the summons and complaint to an agent authorized to receive service on the defendant's behalf.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(c), (e), (h) (service of process upon an individual and an organization).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of process & notice

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦民事诉讼里的送达程序（service of process），看你能不能直接用州法送达被告。

三秒认题路径：

联邦法院 → 州B开庭 → 先看FRCP 4 → 可用州法送达 → 选A

核心法律规则

FRCP 4（Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 4）的考场意思：联邦案里，个人（individual）和组织（organization）都可以按照“法院所在地州”的送达规则，或者“实际送达地州”的规则来送达。

对个人，还可以把传票与起诉状（summons and complaint）交给本人、交给住处里适当年龄和判断力的同住人，或者交给被授权代收的人。对组织，还可以交给officer、managing or general agent，或其他授权代理人。

所以这题最稳的路子不是猜邮箱或秘书，而是直接走State B的送达规则，因为法院就开在State B。

核心判例： FRCP 4 的标准路径就是“按法院所在地州法或送达地州法送达”，本题据此锁定A最稳。

思维导图

先问：联邦案送达，能不能直接用州法？
YES
FRCP 4允许按法院所在地州或送达地州的规则来送达。
本题事实
法院在State B，所以直接看State B的民诉送达规则。
卡点：不是“谁更方便”，而是“有没有按允许的州法路径送达”。
NO
就不能靠随便把材料塞给秘书、发email，或让当事人自己去送。
再看被告类型：个人 + 组织
个人
本人送达 / 同住成年人代收 / 授权代理人代收。
组织
officer / managing or general agent / 授权代理人；必要时再按州法加邮寄。
结论：本题最佳方法是按State B州法送达，答案选A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是组织和个人，就找秘书、发email，或者让学生自己去送，图省事就行。

但考试真正问的是：FRCP 4 允许的正式送达方式是什么，尤其是能否直接按State B州法来做。

司法考试看的是「程序上有没有合法送达」，不是「看起来有没有把文件递出去」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干显示案件在联邦法院的State B，FRCP 4 允许直接按该州送达规则操作，因此这是最稳的方法。

❌ 概念混淆 | 授权对象误判

✕ B: 把secretaries当成当然授权代理人了，题干根本没给授权。

❌ 法律适用 | 邮件送达误套

✕ C: 直接把emailing当合法送达，FRCP 4并没有默认给你这条路。

❌ 事实误判 | 当事人自送偷换

✕ D: 学生自己是原告，不能亲自送达对方；题目要的是非当事人送达。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看法院所在地，再看FRCP 4允许的州法路径，别被“谁来送”这种表面动作带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：联邦送达先看FRCP 4，州法入口优先；法院在State B，就优先找State B的送达规则。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A foreign exchange student from Germany was on vacation in State B with his host family, all citizens of State A, when their car collided with a truck owned by a company headquartered and incorporated in Germany. The truck was driven by a citizen of State B.
The student and the host family brought a negligence suit against the company and the truck driver in a federal court in State B. The student seeks to recover $200,000 and the family seeks $500,000 in damages. The company and the truck driver have filed a motion to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Is the court likely to grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because actions involving foreign citizens pose a federal question.
choices.B: No, because the requirements for diversity jurisdiction are satisfied.
choices.C: Yes, because the doctrine of forum non conveniens requires that the action be heard in Germany.
choices.D: Yes, because the foreign exchange student and the company are citizens of the same country.

questions.explanation:
Diversity of citizenship examples

(28 U.S.C. § 1332)
Diversity
No diversity
U.S. v. Foreign
v.
U.S. v. Resident noncitizen
v.
U.S. + Foreign v. U.S. + Foreign
v.
Foreign v. Foreign
v.
U.S. v. Resident noncitizen
v.
U.S. + Foreign v. Foreign
v.

Subject-matter jurisdiction refers to a federal court's authority to hear a particular type of case. This jurisdictional requirement can be established through federal-question jurisdiction or diversity jurisdiction. Diversity jurisdiction is established when (1) the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and (2) complete diversity of citizenship exists between the opposing parties. As a result, diverse citizenship exists if the suit is between:

  • U.S. citizens domiciled in the U.S. and foreign citizens
  • U.S. citizens and permanent residents domiciled in different states or
  • U.S. citizens domiciled in different states with foreign citizens as additional parties.

Here, the host family from State A and the German exchange student brought a negligence suit against the truck driver from State B and the German company. Since the suit is between U.S. citizens domiciled in different states with foreign citizens as additional parties, diverse citizenship exists. Additionally, the amount-in-controversy requirement is met because the student seeks $200,000 and the family seeks $500,000 in damages. Therefore, the requirements for diversity jurisdiction are satisfied.

(Choice A) Judicial actions involving foreign citizens do not automatically pose a federal question. The cause of action must arise from the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or a federal statute. Since the negligence action asserted here arises from state law, federal-question jurisdiction does not exist.

(Choice C) The doctrine of forum non conveniens allows, but does not require, a federal court to dismiss or stay a lawsuit if a state or foreign judicial system provides a more convenient forum to hear the case. Additionally, this doctrine is unrelated to subject-matter jurisdiction.

(Choice D) The fact that the foreign exchange student and the company are both German citizens is irrelevant. Diverse citizenship is established since the host family and the truck driver are U.S. citizens domiciled in different states and the foreign citizens are additional parties.

📌 Educational Objective

Diverse citizenship exists in a suit between (1) U.S. citizens domiciled in the U.S. and foreign citizens, (2) U.S. citizens and permanent residents domiciled in different states, or (3) U.S. citizens domiciled in different states with foreign citizens as additional parties.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a) (diversity jurisdiction).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 628 (2020) (explaining that diverse citizenship exists in a suit between U.S. citizens domiciled in different states with foreign citizens as additional parties).

该学生和寄宿家庭在B州的联邦法院对该公司和卡车司机提起了过失诉讼。该学生寻求20万美元的损害赔偿，其家庭寻求50万美元的损害赔偿。该公司和卡车司机已提出动议，以缺乏属事管辖权为由请求驳回诉讼。

法院是否可能批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为涉及外国公民的诉讼构成了一个联邦问题。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为已经满足了多元管辖权的要求。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为 forum non conveniens（不方便法院）原则要求该诉讼在德国审理。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该交换生和该公司都是德国公民。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Diversity jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多元国籍管辖（diversity jurisdiction）里，外国人、不同州公民和金额要件放在一起时，联邦法院能不能立案。

三秒认题路径：

先看国籍 → 再看州别 → 再看金额 → 完整多元 → 可受理

核心法律规则

多元国籍管辖（diversity jurisdiction）要求两件事：争议金额超过 $75,000，而且双方之间要有完全多元（complete diversity）。考试里你只要记住：U.S. 公民（U.S. citizens）、外籍公民（foreign citizens）、以及不同州的公民可以组合出多元，但不是“只要有外国人就一定没管辖”。

本题里，德国交换学生和德国家公司虽然都是德国人，但这不自动打掉管辖；关键是美国当事人分属不同州，而且外国人只是额外当事人，仍可满足多元。

核心判例： 28 U.S.C. § 1332 的规则就是：不同州美国公民 + 外国当事人，且金额过线时，通常可以成立多元国籍管辖。

思维导图

原告组 德国学生 + A州家庭
→
被告组 B州司机 + 德国公司
→
先过两关 金额 $200k / $500k
→
关键结论 A州 vs B州 + 外国人只是附加
先问：有没有 完全多元（complete diversity）？
YES：美国公民分属不同州，外籍当事人只是附加 → 继续看金额。
金额：学生要 $200,000，家庭要 $500,000 → 都超过 $75,000。
结论：联邦法院有 subject-matter jurisdiction，不能因缺乏管辖而驳回。
误区：“德国对德国”不是本题的杀点，foreign citizens 不会自动消灭多元。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然有德国学生、德国公司，题目又在说外国人，那就一定没有联邦管辖。

但考试真正问的是：美国当事人是不是分属不同州，而且金额有没有过 $75,000。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的干扰点就是把“出现外国人”误读成“必然无管辖”；其实外国人还可能是多元结构里的附加一层，不是自动否定器。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里美国当事人分属 A、B 两州，且 $200,000 + $500,000 都过线，所以多元国籍管辖成立，法院不该因无 subject-matter jurisdiction 驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把外国当事人当成federal question，其实诉因只是州法过失。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 把 forum non conveniens 当成管辖门槛了，它只是便利性工具。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: 盯着“德国对德国”忽略了美国当事人已构成跨州多元。

这题建议用什么方法？

先扫主体国籍，再扫金额，最后只看有没有“完全多元”这个门槛。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely” 适合中间上诉；但本题不是上诉题，而是 多元国籍管辖（diversity jurisdiction） 题。看到外国人先别慌，先问：美国当事人是否跨州、金额是否过线。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A man domiciled in State A died from complications during surgery at a hospital incorporated and with its principal place of business in State A. The medical license of the surgeon performing the operation was suspended at the time the surgery was performed. The man's legal representative, who was domiciled in State B, sued the hospital on behalf of the man's estate in a state court in State B. The complaint asserted a negligence claim to recover $60,000 and a breach-of-contract claim to recover $40,000. The hospital removed the case to a federal court in State B. The representative filed a motion to remand.
Under State B law, claims for negligence and breach of contract survive the death of a person.
How is the federal court likely to proceed?

choices.A: Remand the case, because the amount-in-controversy requirement is not satisfied.
choices.B: Remand the case, because the parties are not diverse.
choices.C: Retain the case, because the case was properly removed to federal court.
choices.D: Retain the case, because the federal court has supplemental jurisdiction over the claims.

questions.explanation:
A defendant has the power to remove a case from state court to federal court if the case falls within the federal court's original subject-matter jurisdiction. If such jurisdiction does not exist, the federal court must remand the case back to state court. Original jurisdiction can be established through federal-question jurisdiction (not seen here) or diversity jurisdiction, which requires:

  • an amount in controversy exceeding $75,000 and
  • complete diversity of citizenship between the opposing parties.

Citizenship is usually determined by the domiciles of the named parties to the suit. However, the citizenship of a legal representative is determined by the domicile of the minor, legally incompetent person, or decedent on whose behalf the legal representative acts.

Here, the deceased man's legal representative sued the hospital on behalf of the man's estate in state court. The hospital removed the case to federal court. The representative is a citizen of State A because that is where the man was domiciled. The hospital is also a citizen of State A because it is incorporated and has its principal place of business there. Since the opposing parties are both State A citizens, the court lacks diversity (and subject-matter) jurisdiction. Removal was therefore improper, and the federal court will likely remand the case (Choice C).

(Choice A) To satisfy the amount-in-controversy requirement, a single plaintiff can aggregate (ie, combine) claims asserted against a single defendant. Here, the legal representative's complaint satisfies this requirement because the aggregated claims amount to $100,000 ($60,000 for negligence + $40,000 for breach of contract).

(Choice D) When a dispute involves multiple claims and only some fall within the court's original subject-matter jurisdiction, supplemental jurisdiction may exist over the remaining claims. Here, no claim satisfies original subject-matter jurisdiction, so supplemental jurisdiction is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

For purposes of diversity jurisdiction, the citizenship of a legal representative is determined by the domicile of the minor, legally incompetent person, or decedent on whose behalf the legal representative acts.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332(c)(2) (citizenship of legal representative).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1441 (removal requirements).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1447(c) (remand requirements).

根据B州法律，过失和违约的索赔权在当事人死亡后仍然有效。

联邦法院可能会如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 发回案件，因为未满足争议金额的要求。
zh-choices.B: 发回案件，因为各方当事人不具有身份多元性。
zh-choices.C: 保留案件，因为该案件被正确地移送至联邦法院。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Subject-matter jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：遗产法定代表人（legal representative）做多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction）时，国籍要看被代表的被继承人（decedent），不是看代表人自己。

三秒认题路径：

代表起诉 → 看谁算国籍 → 看被代表人 → 双方同州 → 不能多元 → 退回州法院

核心法律规则

移送（removal）只能建立在联邦法院有原始标的管辖权（subject-matter jurisdiction）上；没有原始管辖权，就要发回（remand）。多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction）要求金额超过75,000美元，而且双方必须完全多元（complete diversity）。

对法定代表人（legal representative）来说，考试上国籍不看代表人自己，而看他所代表的未成年人（minor）、无行为能力人（legally incompetent person）或被继承人（decedent）的住所地（domicile）。所以这题的关键不是医院赔多少钱，而是双方是不是都算 State A 公民。

核心判例： 28 U.S.C. § 1332(c)(2) 直接把法定代表人的国籍绑定到被代表的死者；本题因此按被继承人的 domicile 认定，立刻打掉多元管辖。

思维导图

先问：联邦法院能不能留案？
1.先看原始管辖权（original subject-matter jurisdiction）
A.联邦问题（federal question）？题干没有。
B.多元管辖（diversity）？继续查。
2.多元管辖两把锁：
① 金额 > $75,000：这题 $60,000 + $40,000 可合并，金额其实够
② 双方完全多元：法定代表人按死者 domicile 记国籍，死者在 State A
3.医院：State A 公民；代表人：也按死者算 State A 公民。
同州对同州 → 不满足 complete diversity → 无原始管辖权 → 必须 remand
结论：选 B，不是看金额，而是看国籍锁死了。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：100,000 美元已经超过 75,000，应该能留在联邦法院。

但考试真正问的是：完全多元（complete diversity）有没有。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「金额看起来够不够大」。

这里最容易被骗的是把法定代表人（legal representative）当成自己单独算国籍；其实他只是替被继承人（decedent）出面，国籍跟着死者走。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

代表人按死者的 domicile 算国籍，死者和医院都属于 State A，所以没有完全多元，联邦法院应当发回州法院。

❌ 事实误判 | 金额偷看错位

✕ A: 只盯着 amount in controversy，漏掉国籍才是致命点。

❌ 法律适用 | 移送前提误判

✕ C: 把 properly removed 当真了，但原始管辖权根本没成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 补充管辖混用

✕ D: 想用 supplemental jurisdiction 补救，但这里连一个能站住的原始主张都没有。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先查多元国籍，再看金额，最后才考虑能不能移送和发回。

考场速记

记住一句：法定代表人（legal representative）的多元国籍，跟着被代表的被继承人（decedent）走，不跟代表人自己走。

本题再记一个快招：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉口诀，但这题不是上诉题；它只是在提醒你，考试先看规则门槛，再看例外。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An employee filed an employment discrimination suit in federal court against a corporation without the assistance of an attorney. After filing suit, the employee was severely injured in a car accident and hospitalized for three months. Immediately upon being released from the hospital, the employee hired an attorney to represent her in the discrimination suit. The attorney then had the corporation served with process 100 days after the employee's complaint had been filed. The corporation moved to dismiss for improper service of process.
Is the court likely to grant the corporation's motion?

choices.A: No, because the corporation was served with process within 90 days after the employee hired an attorney.
choices.B: No, because the employee can show good cause for the untimely service of process.
choices.C: Yes, because the corporation was not served with process within 90 days after the complaint was filed.
choices.D: Yes, because the delay in service of process was not caused by the corporation's misconduct.

questions.explanation:
Time limit for domestic service of process (FRCP 4(m))
π served Δ < 90 days
after complaint filed?
— Yes →Service is proper
↓
π shows good cause
for untimely service?
  • Sudden illness/injury
  • Natural disaster/catastrophe
  • Misconduct/evasion by Δ
— Yes →Extend time for service
for appropriate period
↓
Dismiss without prejudice
OR
Order service within
specified time

A plaintiff must provide a defendant with notice of a lawsuit through service of process. A defendant in the U.S. must be served with process within 90 days after the plaintiff's complaint is filed.* Here, service of process was untimely because the corporation was served 100 days after the employee filed her complaint. This would generally require the court—by motion or on its own initiative after notifying the plaintiff—to dismiss the action without prejudice OR order service of process within a specified time.

However, if the plaintiff provides good cause as to why service was untimely, the court must extend the time for service for an appropriate period. Good cause exists if service was delayed due to matters outside of the plaintiff's control (eg, sudden illness or injury)—not the plaintiff's own mistake or ignorance. Since the employee here was severely injured and hospitalized for three months after filing the complaint, good cause exists. Therefore, the court will likely deny the corporation's motion to dismiss (Choice C).

*The 90-day deadline for service of process applies to defendants in the U.S. For defendants in a foreign country, most federal courts require that process be served with due diligence.

(Choice A) The deadline for service of process is measured from the date the complaint is filed—not the date the plaintiff hires an attorney. That is because parties are not required to hire an attorney and can proceed pro se (ie, without legal counsel).

(Choice D) A defendant's misconduct provides good cause for untimely service of process. Although there is no indication that the corporation engaged in any misconduct, good cause exists since the employee's serious injury and hospitalization prevented her from serving the corporation within 90 days.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant in the U.S. must be served with process within 90 days after the plaintiff files the complaint unless good cause exists for missing this deadline. If good cause is shown, the court must extend the time for service of process for an appropriate period.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(m) (deadline for service of process).
  • Floyd v. United States, 900 F.2d 1045, 1047 (7th Cir. 1990) (explaining that good cause exists for untimely service of process when extenuating factors such as a sudden illness occur).

一名雇员在没有律师协助的情况下，向联邦法院对一家公司提起了雇佣歧视诉讼。提起诉讼后，该雇员在一场车祸中受重伤，并住院三个月。从医院出院后，该雇员立即聘请了一名律师在歧视诉讼中代理她。该律师随后在雇员的起诉状提交100天后，向该公司送达了诉讼文书。该公司以诉讼文书送达不当为由，请求驳回起诉。

法院是否可能批准该公司的请求？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为在雇员聘请律师后的90天内，公司已被送达诉讼文书。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为雇员可以为未能及时送达诉讼文书提出正当理由。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为在起诉状提交后的90天内，公司未被送达诉讼文书。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为诉讼文书送达的延迟并非由公司的行为不当所致。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦民事诉讼规则 4(m)（FRCP 4(m)）下，90天送达期限（90-day service deadline）没赶上时，法院会不会因为正当理由（good cause）而继续给时间。

三秒认题路径：

起诉后送达 → 超过90天 → 有正当理由？ → 法院延长期限 → 不准驳回

核心法律规则

被告在美国境内时，必须在起诉状提交后 90天（90 days） 内完成 送达诉讼文书（service of process）。如果没在期限内送达，法院通常可以 无偏见驳回（dismiss without prejudice），或者命令在指定时间内完成送达。

但如果原告能证明 正当理由（good cause），比如突发重病、受伤、自然灾害，法院就必须把送达时间延长到合适的期限。这里原告车祸重伤并住院三个月，属于典型的外部障碍，所以不会因为超期送达而直接被驳回。

核心判例： Floyd v. United States — 突发疾病或伤害这类外部原因，可以构成超期送达的 good cause。

思维导图

先看：是否在90天内送达？
Yes → 送达有效，法院不用因为时限问题驳回。
No → 进入 good cause 检查。
有没有外部原因挡住原告？
严重受伤、住院、自然灾害、被告躲避送达 → 有 good cause，法院要延长期限
只是忘了、搞错了、没注意期限 → 没 good cause，法院可无偏见驳回或限期送达。
本题结论：100天送达确实超期，但三个月住院把 good cause 直接点亮。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：100天已经超过90天，所以一定要赢。
但考试真正问的是：原告为什么没能及时送达，是不是有 good cause。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里最容易被带偏的是把“请了律师”当成起算点，或者把“被告没做坏事”当成判断标准；这两句都不是 FRCP 4(m) 的核心。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 三个月重伤住院 是典型外部障碍，构成 good cause，所以法院应延长送达时间，不会直接准许驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 起算点看错

✕ A: 把 hired an attorney 当起算点，送达期限其实从起诉日算。

❌ 法律适用 | 机械超期推导

✕ C: 只盯着 90 days，忘了 good cause 可以把期限拉长。

❌ 事实误判 | 归责对象偷换

✕ D: 把责任硬扣在被告身上，但本题的延迟是原告受伤住院造成的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看起诉后送达是否超期，再立刻问有没有 good cause；程序期限题先抓起算点和例外。

考场速记

记忆口诀：起诉日起算 90 天；有 good cause，就能延长。 这题别死盯“有没有律师”，要先盯“有没有外部原因挡住送达”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A shoe company was incorporated in State A, maintains its headquarters in State B, and stores most of its inventory in State C. At a sales convention in a foreign country, one of the shoe company's corporate officers allegedly assaulted an employee of a shoe distributor. This employee is domiciled in State C.
The employee sued the shoe company in a federal court in State C for the actions of its corporate officer. The shoe company filed a motion to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.
Will the court likely grant the shoe company's motion?

choices.A: No, because the shoe company has minimum contacts with State C.
choices.B: No, because the shoe company is domiciled in State C.
choices.C: Yes, because no state has personal jurisdiction over this claim since it is based on events that occurred in a foreign country.
choices.D: Yes, because the employee's claim does not arise out of the shoe company's contacts with State C and the shoe company is not domiciled in State C.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for personal jurisdiction

(minimum contacts)

14. Forum selection clause:
All parties consent to exclusive
jurisdiction and venue in the state and
federal courts of Texas.

A court must have personal jurisdiction—ie, authority over the parties (or property) before it—to hear a dispute. Personal jurisdiction can be established through specific jurisdiction, which exists when:

  • the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and
  • the exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

These requirements are met if the defendant's contacts with the forum state were so purposeful and substantial that the defendant could have reasonably anticipated being sued in that state (ie, purposeful availment). Here, the State C federal court lacks specific jurisdiction because the employee's claim arises from the corporate officer's actions in the foreign country—not the company's minimum contacts (storing inventory) with State C (Choice A).

However, personal jurisdiction can also be established through general jurisdiction. This exists when the defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" in that state. Home is where the defendant is domiciled. For a corporation, this is (1) the state where it was incorporated and (2) the state where it maintains its principal place of business.

Here, the shoe company was incorporated in State A and has its principal place of business in State B. And though the company conducts business and stores inventory in State C, this is not where the company is domiciled (Choice B). Therefore, the State C federal court lacks general jurisdiction over the company and will likely grant its motion to dismiss.

(Choice C) No state has specific jurisdiction over this claim because it is based on events that occurred in the foreign country. But States A and B would have general jurisdiction over this claim since the shoe company is domiciled there.

(Choice D) Yes, because the employee's claim does not arise out of the shoe company's contacts with State C and the shoe company is not domiciled in State C.

📌 Educational Objective

Specific jurisdiction exists when the claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's contacts with the forum state such that the exercise of personal jurisdiction complies with fair play and substantial justice. General jurisdiction exists when the defendant's contacts with the forum state make the defendant "at home" there.

📚 References
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the requirements for specific jurisdiction).
  • Goodyear Dunlop Tires Operations, S.A. v. Brown, 564 U.S. 915, 926–29 (2011) (discussing the continuous and systematic contacts required for general jurisdiction).

一家鞋业公司在State A注册成立，其总部设在State B，并将其大部分库存存放在State C。在某外国的一次销售会议上，该鞋业公司的一名公司高管据称袭击了一家鞋业经销商的雇员。该雇员的定居地在State C。

该雇员因其公司高管的行为，在State C的联邦法院对该鞋业公司提起了诉讼。该鞋业公司以缺乏对人管辖权为由，提出了驳回起诉的动议。

法院是否可能批准该鞋业公司的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该鞋业公司与State C有最低限度的联系。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该鞋业公司的定居地在State C。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该诉讼请求是基于在外国发生的事件，所以没有一个州对此拥有对人管辖权。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该雇员的诉讼请求并非源于鞋业公司与State C的联系，且该公司的定居地也不在State C。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告公司在 State C 有库存，不等于本案就能在 State C 被起诉；要看 特定管辖（specific jurisdiction） 或 一般管辖（general jurisdiction） 是否成立。

三秒认题路径：

先看是否相关 → 再看是否在家 → 库存不够 → 事发境外 → 选 D

核心法律规则

特定管辖（specific jurisdiction） 的关键是：原告的请求必须起因于或紧密关联被告在该州的 minimum contacts（最低联系），考试上就是“这件事是不是从这个州的联系里长出来的”。

一般管辖（general jurisdiction） 要求被告与论坛州有持续、系统的联系，达到“at home”的程度；公司通常只在注册州和主要营业地才算“家”。

所以，State C 里放库存，只能帮你想到联系，不足以自动让公司在这里“在家”；而这起袭击发生在外国，和 State C 的库存没有直接连接，所以 State C 法院既没有特定管辖，也没有一般管辖。

核心判例： Bristol-Myers Squibb — 说明特定管辖必须和本案请求本身有连接；Goodyear — 说明一般管辖看的是“at home”。

思维导图

先问：State C 法院有没有 personal jurisdiction？
1）特定管辖？ 这起 claim 要从 State C 的 contacts 长出来。
本题答案：否。袭击发生在外国，不是库存导致的争议。
2）一般管辖？ 公司要“at home”——注册地或主要营业地。
本题答案：否。公司在 State A 注册、State B 设总部，State C 只是放库存。
3）结论： State C 法院不能管，motion to dismiss 应该准许。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司在 State C 存了很多货，又有受害人住在这里，所以应该“联系很够”。

但考试真正问的是：这起案件是不是从 State C 的联系里来的，以及公司是不是在 State C “at home”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

换句话说，库存这种背景事实很像烟雾弹；它能让你想到联系，但不能替代“请求与联系之间的连接”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里真正的致命点是：袭击发生在外国，不是从 State C 的库存联系里长出来；而公司也不在 State C “at home”，所以法院会准许驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 最低联系误认

✕ A: 把 minimum contacts 当成万能钥匙了，但这里缺的是“请求与联系的对应”。

❌ 事实误判 | 注册地偷换

✕ B: 直接把 State C 说成公司“家”，但注册地和总部根本不在这里。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对化推断

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A bank sued a foreign investor for fraud in a federal court in State A. The bank was unable to ascertain the investor's primary address for 120 days after filing its complaint, but immediately thereafter mailed the investor a copy of the summons and complaint through certified mail to that address. The investor, upon receipt of the summons and complaint, retained counsel in State A.
State A permits service of process on an individual outside its borders by mailing the summons and complaint to the individual's primary residence. The foreign country where the investor resides is not a signatory to any international agreement that provides service-of-process rules, and there is no applicable federal statute. The foreign country does not permit service by mail.
The investor has moved to dismiss the suit for improper service of process.
What is the investor's best argument in support of the motion to dismiss?

choices.A: The bank did not request that the federal court send a letter rogatory.
choices.B: The bank served the summons and complaint more than 45 days after filing its complaint with the court.
choices.C: The foreign country does not permit service by mail.
choices.D: The investor can only be served by an internationally agreed method of service.

questions.explanation:
Methods of serving process in foreign country
Individual or
organization
  • Following international agreement reasonably calculated to give notice
  • If no international agreement & not prohibited by federal law:
    • following foreign country's rules
    • as foreign country directs in response to letter rogatory or
    • unless prohibited by foreign country, by personal delivery* or mail with request for signed return receipt
  • Following court order, unless prohibited by international agreement
Foreign
government
  • Following special arrangement between plaintiff & foreign state
  • If no special arrangement, by international convention
  • If no convention, by mail to head of foreign affairs ministry with request for signed return receipt
  • If service by mail cannot be made within 30 days, by sending two copies to U.S. Secretary of State via mail requiring signed receipt

*Organizations cannot be served by personal delivery in foreign countries.

A plaintiff must give a defendant notice of a lawsuit through service of process—ie, delivery of the summons and complaint. Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 4(f), a defendant who is an individual can be served in a foreign country by any internationally agreed method of service that is reasonably calculated to give notice (Choice D). However, if there is no such method and no applicable federal law (as seen here), then the defendant can be served:

  • by following the foreign country's rules for service of process
  • as the foreign country directs in response to a letter rogatory—ie, a letter from a domestic court asking a foreign court for assistance or
  • by delivering the summons and complaint to the defendant personally or by mail with a request for a signed return receipt (eg, certified mail)—unless prohibited by the foreign country.*

Here, the bank served the investor with a copy of the summons and complaint by certified mail. However, this method of service is prohibited by the foreign country. Therefore, this is the investor's best argument in support of the motion to dismiss.

*An individual in a foreign country can also be served by any other court-ordered method that does not violate an international agreement.

(Choice A) While asking the foreign country for assistance through a letter rogatory is one method to properly serve a foreign defendant, it is not the only method.

(Choice B) Absent good cause, a defendant located in the U.S. must be served with process within 90 days (not 45 days) after the complaint is filed. However, this 90-day deadline does not apply to a defendant located in a foreign country. Instead, most federal courts require that the plaintiff exercise due diligence in attempting to serve such a defendant.

📌 Educational Objective

When no internationally agreed method of service or applicable federal law exists, an individual defendant in a foreign country can be served (1) by following the foreign country's service-of-process rules, (2) as the foreign country directs in response to a letter rogatory, or (3) by delivering process to the defendant personally or by mail—if permitted by the foreign country.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(f) (service on individual in foreign country).

如果投资者以司法文书送达不当为由请求驳回诉讼，法院是否可能批准该请求？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为银行遵守了A州的司法文书送达规则。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为投资者已经知悉该诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of process & notice

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：外国境内个人（individual in a foreign country）的送达方式里，挂号/认证邮件（mail with signed return receipt）到底能不能用。

三秒认题路径：

外国被告 → 无条约 → 无联邦法 → 只能看4(f) → 邮寄被禁

核心法律规则

抓住这一条就够了

联邦民事诉讼规则 4(f)（Rule 4(f)）管的是外国境内的个人送达。考场意思：先看有没有国际条约；没有的话，再看外国本国规则、letter rogatory，或者在该国不禁止时用个人送达或邮寄。

所以本题里，银行虽然用了certified mail，但题目明说外国不允许邮寄送达，这一步直接卡死。能送达不等于这种方式在该国允许。

核心判例： 没有必须背诵的单独最高法院案名；本题按 Rule 4(f) 的顺序判断即可，关键就是“外国国法是否禁止邮寄”。

思维导图

先问：被告是不是在外国境内的个人？
是进入 Rule 4(f)。
1) 有国际条约吗？
有按条约送达。
无继续看外国规则 / letter rogatory / 邮寄或个人送达。
2) 外国是否禁止邮寄？
本题卡点：foreign country does not permit service by mail → 邮寄这条路被堵死。
否才可用认证邮件。
是不能靠 certified mail 成功送达。
结论：最佳撤诉理由 = 题干送达方式被外国法禁止。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然银行最终把 summons and complaint 送到了，被告也找了律师，那应该已经“通知到了”。

但考试真正问的是：这次送达是不是按规则允许的方式完成，而不是事后有没有真的知道诉讼。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 foreign country does not permit service by mail 直接击中 Rule 4(f) 的限制；银行用认证邮件送达被禁止，所以被告有最强撤诉理由。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 letter rogatory 当成唯一途径了。

❌ 事实误判 | 期限数字偷换

✕ B: 把国内 45 days 期限硬套到外国送达上了。

❌ 法律适用 | 条约条件套错

✕ D: 以为没有条约就只能用 internationally agreed 方法。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序先行：先查是否外国个人送达，再按 4(f) 顺序排除被外国法禁止的方式。

考场速记

记忆口诀：外国个人送达先看条约，再看外国规则；没条约、没联邦法时，mail 可以用，但前提是外国不禁。本题一听见 service by mail 被禁止，答案就锁定在 C。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A bank from State A filed a debt-collection action against a man from State B in a state court located in State A. The bank alleged that the man was liable for credit card charges totaling $80,000. The man filed an answer in which he asserted a counterclaim against the bank. He also joined a credit card company from State A to his counterclaim. The credit card company filed a notice of removal with the federal court in State A. The man moved to remand the action.
How will the court likely rule on the man's motion to remand?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the federal court has exclusive jurisdiction over the action.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the federal court has subject-matter jurisdiction over the action.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the credit card company is not qualified to remove the action.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the man did not consent to the action's removal.

questions.explanation:
Requirements for removal to federal court
Federal court has original
jurisdiction over π’s claims
Federal question
Arises under U.S. Constitution,
treaty, or federal law
Diversity
Amount in controversy >$75,000
& diversity of citizenship
No Δ is citizen of state where
case was originally filed
All Δs consent to removal
Notice filed in federal court within
30 days of initial complaint or
summons; copy delivered to
parties & state court
Removal permitted

π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant

A defendant has the power to remove a case from state court to federal court when the case falls within the federal court's original, subject-matter jurisdiction—which must be established on the face of the plaintiff's complaint—can arise from either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – when a claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not seen here) or
  • diversity jurisdiction – when the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states.*

However, the federal court should remand the case back to state court if there was a procedural error in the removal. Since only defendants listed in the complaint may remove a case, a procedural error occurs when a case is removed by a party other than a defendant. This includes a party joined to the suit by a defendant's counterclaim.

Here, diversity jurisdiction exists because (1) the amount in controversy is $80,000 and (2) the man is from State B while the bank and credit card company are from State A (Choice B). But since the credit card company joined by the man's counterclaim, it is not qualified to remove the action to federal court. Therefore, the court will likely grant the man's motion to remand the case.

*After removal, if a plaintiff seeks to join additional defendants who would destroy diversity jurisdiction, the federal court may deny joinder and proceed with the case OR permit joinder and remand the case to state court.

(Choice A) Federal and state courts have concurrent jurisdiction over state and federal law claims unless the Constitution or Congress expressly provides federal courts with exclusive jurisdiction (not seen here).

(Choice D) When a case has more than one defendant, the consent of all defendants must be obtained before the case can be removed from state to federal court. But here, the man is the only defendant, so the fact that he did not consent to the action's removal is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

Only defendants listed in the plaintiff's complaint have the power to remove a case from state to federal court. A party joined to the suit through a counterclaim is not considered a defendant for removal purposes.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1441 (removal requirements).
  • Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. v. Jackson, 139 S. Ct. 1743, 1748–50 (2019) (holding that only defendants listed in the plaintiff's complaint may remove a case from state to federal court).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Subject-matter jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：移送（removal）时，只有原告起诉状里写明的被告（defendant）才有资格把案子从州法院移到联邦法院；被反诉中拉进来的第三方公司不能自己移走。

三秒认题路径：

谁在移送 → 是不是被告 → 起诉状被告？ → Home Depot → 不能移送

核心法律规则

联邦法院要先有原始管辖权（original jurisdiction），移送才可能成立；这题里虽然 金额争议（amount in controversy） 满足多元国籍管辖，但还要看是谁来移送。

移送（removal）的资格只给原告起诉状里列明的被告（defendant）；被反诉带进来的公司，不算这个规则里的“被告”，所以它没有权力把案件移走。

所以这题不是在问“联邦法院有没有管辖权”，而是在问“这个人有没有资格移送”；资格错了，案子就要发回州法院（remand）。

核心判例： Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. v. Jackson — 只有原告起诉状里的被告能移送；反诉里新加进来的公司不能移送。

思维导图

先问：谁在申请移送？
如果是原告起诉状中的被告
再看联邦是否有原始管辖权？
有联邦问题 / 多元国籍
本题第三关卡：移送主体不合格
结论：不能靠这家公司移送
如果是反诉里后来加入的公司
不是起诉状被告 → 没有 removal 权
直接走向：准许 remand
题干触发点：银行是原告；公司是被反诉加入
答案：C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 $80,000 已经超过门槛，而且双方还看起来是不同州公民，那联邦法院应该能收案。

但考试真正问的是：谁有资格把案子移上去，不是联邦法院抽象上有没有原始管辖权。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里移送的人是反诉中加入的 credit card company，它不是起诉状里的被告；按 Home Depot，它没资格移送，所以应当发回州法院。

❌ 概念混淆 | 专属错因

✕ A: 把exclusive jurisdiction想成本题，但这题根本不是独占管辖。

❌ 法律适用 | 资格规则误搬

✕ B: 只看到多元管辖就忽略了who may remove。

❌ 事实误判 | 共同被告偷换

✕ D: 把all defendants套进来，但这案子里被告不是“多个”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看移送主体，再看资格；有管辖权不等于有移送权。

考场速记

记住一句：原始管辖权只是门票，移送资格（removal standing）才是钥匙；只有起诉状里的被告能开门。

速记：“起诉状里的被告才能移送，反诉里被拉进来的公司不算数。”

An artist from State A sold his paintings over the internet to an art collector from State B. The total purchase price amounted to $80,000. If the collector seeks to remove the case to a federal court in State B, is she likely to succeed?

choices.B: No, because the collector is not qualified to remove the case to federal court.

Removal permitted

π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant

Only a defendant has the power to remove a case from state to federal court when the case falls within the federal court’s original subject-matter jurisdiction. Original jurisdiction, which must be established on the face of a plaintiff’s complaint, can arise from either:

  • diversity jurisdiction – when the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states or
  • federal-question jurisdiction – when the plaintiff asserts a claim that arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law.

Here, the collector (plaintiff) sued the artist (defendant) in state court. The artist then filed a counterclaim that alleged a violation of a federal statute prohibiting fraud in sales across state lines. But as the Supreme Court held in Shamrock Oil & Gas Corp. v. Sheets, a defendant’s counterclaim does not transform the plaintiff into a defendant for removal purposes.* Since the collector remains the plaintiff for removal purposes, she is not qualified to remove the case to federal court (Choice C).

Even the artist, as the defendant, could not remove this case since the collector’s complaint did not establish original jurisdiction. Her breach-of-contract claim arises under state (not federal) law, so the federal court lacks federal-question jurisdiction. And though the artist and collector are citizens of different states, the federal court lacks diversity jurisdiction since the collector demanded only $20,000 in damages. The $60,000 demanded in the artist’s counterclaim is not counted in determining whether the amount in controversy is satisfied (Choice D).

*Congress created a narrow exception to this rule when it enacted 28 U.S.C. § 1454, a special removal rule that permits removal by any party (including a plaintiff) when a federal patent or copyright claim is asserted.

(Choice A) The home-court advantage (ie, forum-defendant) rule prohibits removal when the federal court’s original jurisdiction is based on diversity jurisdiction and a defendant is a citizen of the state where the case was filed. But since the collector is the plaintiff, her residence in State B has no bearing on whether removal is proper.

📌 Educational Objective

Only a defendant has the power to remove a case from state to federal court. A defendant’s counterclaim does not transform a plaintiff into a defendant for removal purposes.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1441 (removal requirements).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1446 (removal procedure).
  • Shamrock Oil & Gas Corp. v. Sheets, 313 U.S. 100, 107–08 (1941) (holding that a counterclaim does not change a plaintiff to a defendant for removal purposes).

该艺术家提交了答辩状，声称其所有画作均已妥善交付给收藏家，且收藏家正试图欺诈他。他还依据一项禁止跨州销售中欺诈行为的联邦法规提起了反诉，要求获得60,000美元的赔偿。

如果该收藏家寻求将案件移送至B州的联邦法院，她是否可能成功？

zh-choices.B: 否，因为该收藏家不具备将案件移送至联邦法院的资格。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Removal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：只有被告（defendant） 才能把案件从州法院移送到联邦法院，原告即使收到反诉也不能变成可移送的一方。

三秒认题路径：

谁在移送 → 是不是被告 → 有无原始管辖 → 反诉能否算 → 结论：不能移送

核心法律规则

移送（removal）的入口很窄：先看联邦法院对原告起诉状（plaintiff’s complaint）有没有原始管辖权（original jurisdiction，考场意思：联邦法院一开始就能不能管）。

如果是联邦问题（federal question），必须来自原告自己的州诉请求；如果是多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction），要满足金额超过 $75,000 且双方公民身份不同。

最关键的是：只有被告（only a defendant） 才有移送资格；原告的counterclaim 不会把原告变成被告，也不会把反诉金额算进移送所需的争议金额。

核心判例： Shamrock Oil & Gas Corp. v. Sheets —— 反诉不会把原告变成可移送的被告，所以原告不能靠对方反诉去联邦法院。

思维导图

先问：谁要移送？
YES：是被告
再问：原告起诉状本身有没有联邦原始管辖？
没有原始管辖 → 不能移送
有原始管辖 → 继续看程序与例外
NO：是原告
原告即使被反诉，也通常没有移送资格
本题钉死点：collector 是原告，不是 defendant。
陷阱
artist 的 federal counterclaim 不把 collector 变成可移送的被告
答案走向：B，不能移送。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然有 federal statute 和 $80,000，那就应该能去联邦法院。

但考试真正问的是：谁有资格移送，不是“案子看起来像不像联邦案”。

命题人想骗你把“有联邦因素”误当成“原告也能移送”；其实反诉再强，也不改变原告身份。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干真正的关键是 collector 还是原告；counterclaim 不会给原告移送权，所以她不能把案子移到联邦法院。

❌ 概念混淆 | 论坛被告误判

✕ A: 把 home state 当成关键，但原告的住址不是移送门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 反诉移送误判

✕ C: 以为 counterclaim 能把原告变被告，这正是 Shamrock Oil 禁掉的想法。

❌ 事实误判 | 金额合并偷换

✕ D: 想把 $60,000 反诉额算进去凑金额，但看的是原告起诉状，不是后加的反诉。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看移送主体，再看原始管辖；只要主体不是被告，后面金额再大也先卡死。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“Only a defendant removes.” 先抓“谁能移送”，再抓“原告起诉状有没有原始管辖”。

再补一句：反诉（counterclaim） 不改身份，反诉金额 也通常不算进移送的金额门槛。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A technology company incorporated and headquartered in State A hired an engineer domiciled in State B. The employment contract between the company and the engineer stated that all work product produced by the engineer was owned by the company. While employed by the company, the engineer developed a software program that was unrelated to the company's business. When the engineer left the company, she attempted to sell her program for $50,000.
The technology company sued the engineer in a federal court in State A to enjoin the sale and for a declaratory judgment that the company owned the rights to the software program. The company claimed that it could incorporate the program into its business and increase profits by $100,000. The engineer defended on the ground that the contract does not apply to work that is unrelated to the company's business.
The case proceeded to trial. After the close of evidence, the engineer moved to dismiss the case for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Should the court grant the engineer's motion?

choices.A: No, because the engineer waived this defense by failing to assert it before the close of evidence.
choices.B: No, because the parties are diverse and the value of the requested relief exceeds $75,000.
choices.C: Yes, because the company failed to demand damages in addition to the requested relief.
choices.D: Yes, because the cost to the engineer to comply with the requested relief is only $50,000.

questions.explanation:
Subject-matter jurisdiction is established when a federal court has federal-question jurisdiction (not seen here) or diversity jurisdiction over a particular case. Diversity jurisdiction exists when the opposing parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

The amount in controversy is generally determined by the monetary damages requested in the plaintiff's complaint. However, it can also be determined when a plaintiff requests equitable relief—eg, declaratory judgment, injunction (both requested here). Since equitable relief has no explicit monetary value, its implicit monetary value is calculated by the larger of the following:

  • the cost to the defendant if forced to comply with the requested equitable relief (eg, lost sales) or
  • the worth to the plaintiff if the requested equitable relief is granted (eg, expected profits).

Here, the parties are diverse because the company is incorporated and headquartered in State A and the engineer is domiciled in State B. The cost to the engineer if forced to comply with the requested equitable relief is only the $50,000 she would lose if her sale is barred. However, the requested equitable relief is worth $100,000 in expected profits to the company, so the amount-in-controversy requirement is satisfied (Choice D). Therefore, diversity jurisdiction exists, and the court should deny the engineer's motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) The right to challenge subject-matter jurisdiction is never waived. Instead, this issue can be raised at any time by the parties or on the court's own initiative (ie, sua sponte).

(Choice C) A plaintiff need not demand damages to satisfy the amount-in-controversy requirement. The reason is that a request for equitable relief can satisfy the amount-in-controversy requirement on its own if the value of the relief—based on its cost to the defendant or worth to the plaintiff—exceeds $75,000.

📌 Educational Objective

In a diversity action, a request for equitable relief satisfies the amount-in-controversy requirement if the value of the relief exceeds $75,000 based on its (1) cost to the defendant or (2) worth to the plaintiff—whichever is larger.

📚 References
  • Hunt v. Wash. State Apple Advert. Comm'n, 432 U.S. 333, 347–48 (1977) (holding that the amount in controversy in an action requesting equitable relief is measured by the value of the object of the litigation).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 962 (2020) (explaining how the amount in controversy is determined in actions that request equitable relief).
questions.zh-question:
一家在A州注册成立并以其为总部的科技公司，雇佣了一位居住在B州的工程师。公司与工程师之间的雇佣合同规定，工程师产生的所有工作成果均归公司所有。在受雇于该公司期间，该工程师开发了一款与公司业务无关的软件程序。当该工程师离开公司时，她试图以50,000美元的价格出售她的程序。

该科技公司在A州的联邦法院起诉该工程师，请求禁止其出售，并请求宣告性判决，确认公司拥有该软件程序的所有权。公司声称，其可以将该程序整合到其业务中，并增加100,000美元的利润。工程师辩称，该合同不适用于与公司业务无关的工作。

案件进入庭审程序。在证据出示结束后，工程师以缺乏属事管辖权为由，动议驳回案件。

法院是否应批准工程师的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为工程师未在证据出示结束前主张此项抗辩，从而放弃了该抗辩。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为双方当事人具有多元性，且所请求的救济价值超过75,000美元。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为公司在请求救济之外，未要求损害赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为工程师遵守所请求的救济的成本仅为50,000美元。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Subject-matter jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦多元管辖里，原告只要请求的是衡平救济（equitable relief），争议金额就看救济的价值是否超过 $75,000。

三秒认题路径：

多元管辖 → 衡平救济 → 看价值 → 取较大值 → 超过7.5万

核心法律规则

多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction）要求：双方公民身份不同，且争议金额超过 $75,000。这里公司在 State A、工程师在 State B，所以完全多元（complete diversity）满足，考点只剩金额。

如果原告要的是禁令（injunction）、宣告判决（declaratory judgment）这类衡平救济（equitable relief），金额不看表面标价，而看两边谁的数更大：对被告的成本（cost to defendant），或 对原告的价值（worth to plaintiff）。考试里取较大那个。

所以本题公司能主张的价值是 $100,000 的预期利润，不是工程师卖软件的 $50,000；金额门槛已经过了，案件不能因缺乏 subject-matter jurisdiction 被驳回。

核心判例： Hunt v. Washington State Apple Advertising Commission — 衡平救济的争议金额按“诉讼标的价值”算，取对原告的价值或对被告的成本中更大者。

思维导图

先问：这是终局性问题吗？
是终局诉讼？
否
再看：
是否多元管辖
→
双方不同州公民
→
金额门槛 > $75,000
金额怎么估？
对被告的成本
卖出被禁，损失只有 $50,000
对原告的价值
可并入业务，预期利润 $100,000
取较大值
卡死点：选更大那个，金额过线
结论：
不能因缺少管辖而撤案 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：工程师卖软件只值 $50,000，是不是金额不够，所以法院没管辖权。

但考试真正问的是：原告请求的是禁令和宣告判决，金额要看救济价值，不是看被告手里那笔交易本身值多少钱。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 injunction 和 declaratory judgment 都是衡平救济，按较大值看争议金额；公司可主张 $100,000，所以多元管辖成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 期限偷换

✕ A: 以为没及时提就waived，但 subject-matter jurisdiction 从来不会被这样放过。

❌ 概念混淆 | 损害赔偿误读

✕ C: 把“没要 damages”当成致命点，其实衡平救济自己就能把金额门槛顶过去。

❌ 法律适用 | 低估值误套

✕ D: 只盯着工程师的 $50,000，漏了还要看公司能赚到的更大价值。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定救济类型，再用“对被告成本 vs 对原告价值”取较大值，最后看是否超过 $75,000。

考场速记

记忆口诀：衡平救济看两边，取大不取小；多元管辖先看州籍，再看金额。

碰到 injunctive relief / declaratory relief，先问“谁赚得更多或谁亏得更多”，不要被表面交易额带跑。
