questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of process & notice

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦官员（federal officer）被起诉为个人身份（individual capacity）时，送达程序（service of process）要按“送达普通个人”的规则走，而不是去送达机构本身。

三秒认题路径：

个人身份起诉 → 官员涉公职 → 按个人送达 → 已亲自送到 → 送达有效

核心法律规则

FRCP 4(i) 处理的是你告联邦官员/雇员（federal officer or employee）时怎么送达。若你告的是个人身份（individual capacity），考场意思：就按送达人规则（rules for serving an individual）去做，像对普通被告那样亲自送达（personal delivery）即可。

同时还要把美国政府（U.S. government）送到位；如果漏了，法院通常给你合理时间（reasonable time）补救，但这不是说个人送达也能随便错。

核心判例： Kentucky v. Graham — 先分清是个人身份还是官方身份；本题是个人身份，所以对人送达有效。

思维导图

起点：你起诉的是联邦官员，问的是送达有没有做对？
先看身份： 个人身份（individual capacity）
→ 规则：按普通个人送达，不是按机构送达。
再看事实： 被告在住所被亲自送达
→ 这正好满足个人送达。
再看政府： 美国政府也已送达
→ 连附加要求也满足了。
卡死结论： 不能说“必须送 IRS 才行”
→ 答案 A：服务有效，不能成功主张送达不当。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然他是IRS agent，那是不是应该先送IRS或只能按政府机关的方式送？

但考试真正问的是：这次是告他个人身份，所以核心只看他有没有按个人规则被送到；题干已经说他在住处被亲自送达了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（本题不是“机关找没找对”，而是“人送没送对”）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A corporation has been the subject of several news reports charging that the pollution emitted by its factory endangers the health of hundreds of residents in a subdivision. The corporation filed an action in federal court against the residents to obtain a declaratory judgment that it complied with environmental regulations and is not responsible for any subsequent harm. A federal statute authorizes this suit.
The state in which the federal court is located permits service of process by mail or by publishing notice of the suit in a newspaper. The corporation obtained the name and address of each resident in the subdivision from the county tax assessor. To avoid the expense of mailing service to each resident individually, the corporation published notice of the suit in the subdivision's community newspaper pursuant to the state's procedural rules.
Did the corporation properly serve the residents with process?

choices.A: No, because service by publication was unreasonable since the corporation knew the name and address of each resident.
choices.B: No, because the residents were not personally served with process.
choices.C: Yes, because service by publication was reasonable due to the expense associated with mailing service to each resident.
choices.D: Yes, because the newspaper publication provided the residents with reasonable notice of the action.

questions.explanation:
Service of process under state procedural rule
(reasonable notice under due process)

Identity and address known / obtainable
= Service by publication unconstitutional
Identity and address unknown / unobtainable
= Service by publication constitutional

A plaintiff must provide the defendant with adequate notice of a lawsuit through service of process, which must comply with both procedural rules and due process. In a federal court action, Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 4 permits service of process on a defendant-individual located in the U.S. by any of the following methods:

  • Personal service – when process is delivered in person to the defendant
  • Substituted service – when process is delivered to the defendant's agent or left at the defendant's dwelling with a resident of suitable age and discretion
  • State procedural rules – when process is served pursuant to the rules of the state where the court sits or service is attempted (as seen with the newspaper publication here) (Choice B)

However, attempted service must also satisfy due process. Under this constitutional requirement, service must reasonably apprise the defendant of the pending suit so that the defendant may appear and present objections. This means that the plaintiff must notify the defendant of the lawsuit by the most reasonable means under the circumstances.

Service by publication is the most reasonable means in the rare instance when the defendant's identity or address is unknown and unobtainable. But if the plaintiff knows or can reasonably obtain this information, a more reasonable means of service must be used (eg, service by mail). Here, the corporation had obtained the residents' names and addresses from the county tax assessor, so service by publication was unreasonable. Therefore, the residents were not properly served with process (Choices C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

A plaintiff must provide the defendant with adequate notice of a lawsuit that reasonably apprises the defendant of the suit so that the defendant may appear and present objections. Service by publication is permitted only when the defendant's identity or address is unknown and unobtainable.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(e) (service of process on individual in the United States).
  • Mullane v. Cent. Hanover Bank & Trust Co., 339 U.S. 306, 319 (1950) (holding that a plaintiff cannot provide notice by publication when the identities and addresses of the defendants are known or easily ascertainable).
  • 62B Am. Jur. 2d Process § 206 (2020) (explaining service by publication).

联邦法院所在州允许通过邮寄或在报纸上刊登诉讼通知的方式送达诉讼文书。该公司从县税务评估员处获得了该小区每位居民的姓名和地址。为避免向每位居民单独邮寄送达的费用，该公司依据该州的程序性规定，在该小区的社区报纸上刊登了诉讼通知。

该公司是否以适当方式向居民送达了诉讼文书？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为在该公司知道每位居民的姓名和地址的情况下，公告送达是不合理的。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为诉讼文书没有亲自送达给居民。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为考虑到向每位居民邮寄送达的相关费用，公告送达是合理的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of process & notice

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州规则允许公告送达（service by publication）时，若对方姓名和地址其实已知或可合理取得，是否仍满足正当程序（due process）。

三秒认题路径：

公告送达 → 姓名地址已知 → 先看更好方式 → 公告不够 → 选 No

核心法律规则

在联邦法院，送达程序（service of process）可以按州规则做，但还得过正当程序（due process）这一关。考场意思：送达必须用最合理、最能让被告知道起诉的方式。

公告送达（service by publication）只有在被告身份或地址unknown and unobtainable时才算合理。考场意思：只要姓名和地址知道或能查到，就该用邮寄或个人送达，而不是只登报。

核心判例： Mullane v. Cent. Hanover Bank & Trust Co. — 知道或容易查到对方姓名地址时，不能只靠公告来送达。

思维导图

先问：送达方式有没有满足“最合理通知”?
第1步：州规则允许登报，但这只是 procedural rule，不是最后答案。
第2步：题干里公司已经从税务评估员拿到每个住户的 name and address。
第3步： 卡死点：既然能合理取得地址，就不能把公告当成“足够合理”的通知。
结论：应选更合理方式（如邮寄/个人送达），所以公告送达失败，答案是 No。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州规则都允许登报，而且公司只是想省钱，所以应该算送达有效。

但考试真正问的是：在正当程序下，这是不是最合理的通知方式；既然姓名和地址已经能拿到，登报就太弱了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干已从税务评估员拿到每个住户姓名和地址，却还只登报；既然有更合理的通知方式，公告送达就不够。

❌ 概念混淆 | 机械个人送达

✕ B: 以为必须亲自送到每个人手里才行。

❌ 法律适用 | 省钱理由误判

✕ C: 把expense当成正当程序理由。

❌ 事实误判 | 通知强度偷换

✕ D: 看到报纸“可能有人会看到”就当成足够通知。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看被告地址是不是已知；已知就直接排除公告送达，别被州规则和省钱理由带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：公告送达只救“找不到人”的情况，不救“懒得找更好方式”的情况。

口诀：known address → no publication；若地址可合理取得，先想到邮寄或个人送达。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A singer, a citizen of State A, believes that her former record label violated federal law when it sold the rights to her songs to another company. The singer has brought a suit in federal court in State A against the record label, which is headquartered and incorporated in a foreign country, and the record label's president, who resides in the foreign country.
What is the best method of serving the defendants?

choices.A: Service as required by State A's rules of civil procedure.
choices.B: Service by having a process server personally deliver copies of the summons and complaint to the record label's headquarters and its president.
choices.C: Service by mailing copies of the summons and complaint to the record label and its president.
choices.D: Service pursuant to an international agreement that is reasonably calculated to give notice.

questions.explanation:
Methods of serving process in foreign country
Individual or
organization
  • Following international agreement reasonably calculated to give notice
  • If no international agreement & not prohibited by federal law:
  • ◦ following foreign country's rules
  • ◦ as foreign country directs in response to letter rogatory or
  • ◦ unless prohibited by foreign country, by personal delivery* or mail with request for signed return receipt
  • Following court order, unless prohibited by international agreement
Foreign
government
  • Following special arrangement between plaintiff & foreign state
  • If no special arrangement, by international convention
  • If no convention, by mail to head of foreign affairs ministry with request for signed return receipt
  • If service by mail cannot be made within 30 days, by sending two copies to U.S. Secretary of State via mail requiring signed receipt
*Organizations cannot be served by personal delivery in foreign countries.

Due process requires that a plaintiff notify the defendant of a lawsuit through service of process—ie, delivery of the summons and complaint. Individuals and organizations located in a foreign country can be served with process by any internationally agreed method of service that is reasonably calculated to give notice under the circumstances. Therefore, the singer's best method of serving the foreign record label and its president is service pursuant to an applicable international agreement that meets that standard.

(Choice A) An individual or organization can be served with process in the U.S. as required by the rules of civil procedure of the forum state—ie, the state in which the court is located. However, this is not a proper method to serve an individual or organization in a foreign country (as seen here).

(Choice B) An individual in a foreign country can generally be served with process by having a process server personally deliver a copy of the summons and complaint to the individual. However, organizations located abroad cannot be served in this manner.

(Choice C) A plaintiff can generally serve process on individuals and organizations in foreign countries through mail requiring a signed receipt (eg, certified mail), but only when there is no internationally agreed means of service.

📌 Educational Objective

Individuals and organizations in foreign countries can be served with process by any internationally agreed method of service that is reasonably calculated to give notice.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(f) & (h)(2) (service of process on individuals and organizations in foreign countries).
  • 4B Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 1134 (4th ed. 2020) (explaining how process can be served on individuals and organizations located abroad).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of Process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：外国当事人怎么送达，先看有没有国际协议（international agreement），有的话优先用它。

三秒认题路径：

外国被告 → 送达方式 → 先看协议 → 再看备选 → 选 D

核心法律规则

被告在外国时，送达程序（service of process）要先找有没有适用的国际协议（international agreement）；只要该方法能合理通知对方，就可以用。合理通知（reasonably calculated to give notice）的意思是：不是看形式最像美国国内送达，而是看能不能真正把诉讼消息送到对方手里。

这里被告是外国公司和其外国总统，所以题目要你选的不是美国州法送达，也不是随便个人递送，而是按可用的国际协议送达。

核心判例： 本题对应 Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(f) & 4(h)(2) 的外国送达规则：先用国际协议，能用就优先用它。

思维导图

被告在外国？
YES： 先问有没有国际协议（international agreement）可用
有协议 → 按协议送达 → 够通知就行
所以本题直接到 D
NO： 才往后看外国规则、委托状、邮件等备选
陷阱： 别把State A rules当成外国送达答案；也别把国内个人送达规则硬套到外国公司。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：只要能把 summons and complaint 送出去，随便用州法、邮寄或个人递送都行。

但考试真正问的是：外国送达有专门顺序，先看国际协议，再看其他备选。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干明确是外国公司和外国总统，foreign country 里送达先看国际协议；这种方法最稳，直接命中规则。

❌ 概念混淆 | 州法套错题

✕ A: 把forum state的程序规则硬套到外国送达。

❌ 事实误判 | 公司个人混送

✕ B: 以为公司和总统都能在外国被personally deliver一把送达。

❌ 法律适用 | 邮寄顺序颠倒

✕ C: 先用了mail，却忽略了有国际协议时它不该排前面。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看被告所在地，再按“国际协议优先”的顺序排除干扰项。

考场速记

记忆口诀：外国被告送达，先找国际协议；有协议先用协议，没协议再看备选。 这类题先盯“外国”，再盯“是否有国际安排”，别被州法和国内送达习惯带跑。

14. Forum selection clause:
All parties consent to
exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the state and
federal courts of Texas.

A court must have personal jurisdiction—i.e., authority over the parties (or property) before the court—to hear a case. If a defendant has not consented to the court's personal jurisdiction or been served with process within the forum state, personal jurisdiction must be established through:

  • general jurisdiction – when the defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" (i.e., where the defendant is domiciled) or
  • specific jurisdiction – when the plaintiff's claim arises from or closely relates to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and the exercise of jurisdiction would comply with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

Here, State C has personal jurisdiction if the defendant was served with process there as the plaintiff sought (Choice C). State A has general jurisdiction because the defendant lives (i.e., is domiciled) there (Choice A). And State D has specific jurisdiction because the plaintiff's claim arises out of the defendant's contact with State D (where the accident occurred) (Choice D). But the plaintiff's claim is unrelated to the defendant's contacts with State B (working and shopping). Therefore, State B is least likely to have personal jurisdiction over the defendant.

📌 Educational Objective

A state must have personal jurisdiction over the parties to hear a case. Personal jurisdiction can be based on (1) consent, (2) service of process in the forum state, (3) general jurisdiction, or (4) specific jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the requirements for specific jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question: 被告居住在A州（State A）。他通勤到邻近的B州（State B）工作，并在那里进行大部分购物（B州没有消费税）。被告每年夏天都会在C州（State C）度假一个月。在从家开车前往C州的途中，被告首次路过D州（State D），并在那里因疏忽撞毁了原告（一名D州公民）价值100,000美元的跑车。被告继续前往C州，并在那里度假了数周。事故发生后的第二天，原告向联邦法院提起诉讼，并试图在次日通过亲自送达（personal service）或邮寄送达（service by mail）的方式向被告送达诉讼文书（serve process）。A州、B州、C州和D州均设有成文法，授权在《美国宪法》（U.S. Constitution）允许的范围内，对在州内从事活动的任何人行使对人管辖权（personal jurisdiction）。在假设对事管辖权（subject-matter jurisdiction）成立的前提下，原告在哪个州最不可能获得对被告的对人管辖权（personal jurisdiction）？

zh-choices.A: A州（State A）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：哪一个州对被告个人管辖（personal jurisdiction）最站不住脚，尤其是一般管辖（general jurisdiction）和特定管辖（specific jurisdiction）能不能搭上。

三秒认题路径：

先看住所 → 再看事故地 → 再看服务送达 → 最后排掉无关州

核心法律规则

法院要先有个人管辖（personal jurisdiction），才能对被告开庭。没有同意（consent）或在论坛州内送达诉状（service of process）时，就要看两条：被告在该州是否“在家（at home）”——这是一般管辖（general jurisdiction）；或者原告的请求是否来自被告在该州的接触——这是特定管辖（specific jurisdiction）。

对特定管辖（specific jurisdiction）来说，关键不是“被告在那州有活动”，而是“这起案子是不是从那次活动长出来的”。如果只是工作、购物这类和事故无关的联系，通常不能把这起事故案子拉进那州法院。

核心判例： Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Superior Court — 特定管辖要求诉因和论坛州联系要对得上，单纯一般性活动不够。

思维导图

先问：这个州能不能对被告管辖？
YES 1： 同意（consent） 或 州内送达 → 直接有管辖
NO： 进入两条主线
A. 一般管辖
State A
被告住在这里 → 通常就是“家” → 有管辖。
State B
只是工作、购物 → 不等于“在家” → 一般管辖过不去。
B. 特定管辖
State D
事故就发生在这里 → 诉因直接来自这次接触 → 能上钩。
State C
如果在这里被送达 → 也能直接建立管辖。
卡死结论：State B 只有工作和购物，和这次事故案子没直接关系，所以最不容易有管辖。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：State B 里有工作、购物，接触看起来很多，应该也能起诉。

但考试真正问的是：这些接触有没有和交通事故（car accident）直接连上；没有连上，就不能拿来撑特定管辖（specific jurisdiction）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

State B 只有工作和购物，而原告的事故请求并不是从这些接触里长出来的，所以最不像有个人管辖（personal jurisdiction）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 住所当成无关

✕ A: 把lives in看漏了，住所州通常就是一般管辖（general jurisdiction）所在地。

❌ 法律适用 | 送达州当成无视

✕ C: 题目给了serve process，在州内送达本身就是一条直接管辖入口。

❌ 事实误判 | 事故地条件漏读

✕ D: 事故正是在这里发生的，原告主张和这个州的接触直接挂钩。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分一般管辖和特定管辖，再只盯“这起事故和这个州有没有直接关系”。

考场速记

记住这句：住所看一般管辖，事故看特定管辖，纯工作购物不够打到事故案。

如果你在题里看到“住哪、在哪出事、在哪被送达”，先按这三步排，不要被背景故事带跑。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Two individuals, both domiciled in State A, created an unincorporated nonprofit organization and promised investors that their monetary contributions would be donated to charities focused on ending world hunger. The contributions were instead used to purchase several properties in State B. The individuals have never physically traveled to and have no other connections with State B, as the properties are approximately 100 miles away from State A.
The federal government filed a civil forfeiture action in a federal district court in State B to seize the properties located there. After being properly served with notice and the complaint, the individuals filed a motion to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.
Should the court grant the motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because a court where the property is being seized always has jurisdiction over the civil forfeiture action.
choices.B: No, because the action is related to the properties located in State B.
choices.C: Yes, because it would be unfair to hale the individuals to court in State B.
choices.D: Yes, because the individuals lack minimum contacts with State B.

questions.explanation:
Types of action for personal jurisdiction
Types of actions
In rem
  • Brought directly against property
  • Determines all persons' interest in property
  • Eg, forfeiture, condemnation
Quasi in rem
  • Brought directly against person in reference to property
Type I
  • Determines parties' interests in property
  • Eg, quiet title
Type II
  • Uses person's property to satisfy unrelated claim
  • Eg, attachment, garnishment
In personam
  • Brought directly against person
  • Adjudicates person's personal liability
  • Eg, intentional tort, negligence

Personal jurisdiction refers to a court's authority over the parties or property in the action before it. There are three types of actions that can be asserted: in rem, quasi in rem, and in personam (see above image). Regardless of the type of action, a federal court's exercise of personal jurisdiction must comport with due process. This constitutional requirement is satisfied when:

  • the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and
  • the exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

Civil forfeiture is an in rem action initiated by the government to seize property used in illegal activity. For in rem actions, minimum contacts almost always exist since these actions relate to property located in the forum state (Choice D). Therefore, the federal court has personal jurisdiction over the individuals' properties in State B and should deny their motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) A court where the property is being seized may not have jurisdiction over the civil forfeiture action in the rare instance that the exercise of jurisdiction does not comply with fair play and substantial justice. This issue typically arises if the seized property was fraudulently brought to the forum state (not seen here).

(Choice C) In civil forfeiture and other in rem actions, the property itself is the defendant. As a result, minimum contacts for personal jurisdiction depend on the location of the property and its relation to the action. Jurisdiction does not depend on the individuals' domicile or their minimum contacts with the forum state (eg, whether it would be unfair to hale them to court in the state).

📌 Educational Objective

A court almost always has personal jurisdiction in an in rem action (eg, civil forfeiture action). Minimum contacts exist because an in rem action relates to property in the forum state. And exercising jurisdiction complies with fair play and substantial justice so long as the plaintiff did not fraudulently bring the property into the forum state.

📚 References
  • Shaffer v. Heitner, 433 U.S. 186, 207–08 (1977) (stating that a court generally has personal jurisdiction when property in the forum state is the source of the underlying controversy between the plaintiff and the defendant).
  • Restatement (Second) of Judgments §§ 5–6 (Am. Law Inst. 1982) (explaining in personam, in rem, and quasi in rem actions).

两名定居在A州的个人成立了一个非法人非营利组织，并向投资者承诺，他们的资金捐助将捐赠给致力于消除世界饥饿的慈善机构。然而，这些捐助款项被用于在B州购买数处房产。由于这些房产距离A州约100英里，这两名个人从未亲身前往B州，也与B州没有其他联系。

联邦政府在B州的联邦地区法院提起了民事没收之诉，旨在没收位于该州的房产。在正式收到通知和起诉状的送达后，这两名个人以缺乏属人管辖权为由，提出了驳回动议。

法院应否批准该驳回动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为没收财产所在地的法院始终对民事没收之诉拥有管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该诉讼与位于B州的房产有关。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为强迫这两名个人到B州应诉是不公平的。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为这两名个人与B州缺乏最低限度的联系。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：civil forfeiture（民事没收） 这种 in rem（对物诉讼），只要财产在州内，法院通常就有 personal jurisdiction（人身管辖），不是看被告本人有没有去过州里。

三秒认题路径：

对物诉讼 → 财产在州内 → 关联该财产 → 不是看人去没去过 → 通常可管

核心法律规则

in rem（对物诉讼） 的考场意思：法院直接盯的是财产，不是先盯这个人。civil forfeiture（民事没收） 就是典型例子。只要被没收的财产就在 forum state（诉讼地州），通常就满足 minimum contacts（最低联系）。

这里再看 due process（正当程序）：只要财产和争议有关，且没有把财产 fraudulently 带入州内，法院一般就能继续管，不会因为当事人本人没去过就丢管辖。

核心判例： Shaffer v. Heitner — 财产若是争议来源，法院通常可以据此取得管辖；本题更直接，因为没收对象就在 State B。

思维导图

先问：这是 final judgment（终局判决） 问题吗？
不是
题干是 civil forfeiture（民事没收），属于 in rem（对物诉讼），先看财产在哪。
关卡
财产在 State B → 争议直接连着州内财产 → minimum contacts（最低联系） 通常成立。
卡死点
不要把“没去过州里”当成致命点；in rem 看的是财产，不是个人旅行史。
结论
法院应拒绝驳回动议，答案走“No”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告从没去过 State B，看起来就“没有联系”，所以法院不该管。

但考试真正问的是：这不是普通 in personam（对人诉讼），而是 in rem（对物诉讼）；法院看的是财产和争议的连接点，不是个人是否亲自到过该州。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 properties located in State B 已把争议财产锚定在本州；civil forfeiture 属 in rem，所以法院通常有管辖。

❌ 概念混淆 | 绝对管辖误判

✕ A: 把“财产在州内”误听成永远自动有管辖。

❌ 法律适用 | 公平感受误判

✕ C: 盯着“看起来不公平”走，但 fair to hale 不是本题的决定点。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看个人足迹

✕ D: 只算被告没去过州里，漏掉了财产本身就在州内这个关键事实。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定诉讼类型，再看财产位置；in rem 题优先抓“财产在哪”，别先盯人的州际接触。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”是中间上诉记忆法；但本题不是上诉题，真正要记的是：in rem（对物诉讼） 先看财产在不在州里。

一句话背法：财产在州内，通常就有管辖；别把“人没去过”当成致命点。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff domiciled in State A brought a wrongful death action in a federal court in State A against a State B parent corporation and one of its foreign subsidiaries. The plaintiff alleged that a tire manufactured by the subsidiary in Europe had caused his wife's death in an automobile accident in Europe.
The parent corporation does significant business throughout the United States, including in State A. The subsidiary conducts no business and has no employees or bank accounts in State A. The subsidiary manufactures its tires for the European market, but 2% of its tires are distributed in State A by the parent corporation. The subsidiary has moved to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.
Should the court grant the subsidiary's motion?

choices.A: No, because 2% of the subsidiary's tires entered State A through the stream of commerce.
choices.B: No, because of the general personal jurisdiction established over the parent corporation.
choices.C: Yes, because the accident did not occur in the United States.
choices.D: Yes, because the subsidiary lacks continuous, systematic, and substantial contacts with State A.

questions.explanation:
Personal jurisdiction
(court's authority over defendant)
Type Requirements
Service of process • Serving process on defendant voluntarily in state where court is located (ie, forum state)
Consent • Express – contractual agreement (eg, forum-selection clause)
• Implied – engaging in specific activity that state has substantial interest in regulating (eg, driving on public roads)
• Waiver – untimely objection to personal jurisdiction
• Appearance – voluntarily appearing in court to litigate merits of case
Specific
(case-linked)		 • Plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to defendant's minimum contacts (ie, purposeful availment) with forum state AND
• Exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play & substantial justice
General
(all-purpose)		 • Defendant has continuous & systematic contacts with forum state so substantial that defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, defendant's domicile)

Personal jurisdiction is established when the defendant consents or is served with process in the forum state (not seen here). It can also be established through specific or general jurisdiction. Specific jurisdiction exists when:

• the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and

• the exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

A defendant manufacturer (eg, the subsidiary) has minimum contacts with the forum state if it places a product in the stream of commerce plus purposefully targets that state. Here, 2% of the subsidiary's tires entered State A through the stream of commerce. But the subsidiary did not purposefully target State A because it did not conduct business or have employees or bank accounts there. Therefore, the court lacks specific jurisdiction (Choice A).

In contrast, general jurisdiction exists when the defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, domiciled) there. Here, the subsidiary has no such contacts with State A because it is domiciled in Europe. Therefore, the court also lacks general jurisdiction over the subsidiary, and it should grant the motion to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.

(Choice B) The court's general jurisdiction over the parent corporation would not give it jurisdiction over the subsidiary unless the subsidiary was acting as the parent corporation's agent or alter ego. Here, the subsidiary did not act as an agent or alter ego because its business (manufacturing tires) is separate from the parent corporation's (distributing tires).

(Choice C) Although the accident occurred outside the United States, the court could have had general jurisdiction over the subsidiary had it had continuous and systematic contacts with State A.

📌 Educational Objective

General jurisdiction over a defendant exists when the defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, domiciled) there.

📚 References
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the minimum contacts required for specific jurisdiction).
  • Goodyear Dunlop Tires Operations, S.A. v. Brown, 564 U.S. 915, 926–29 (2011) (discussing the continuous and systematic business contacts required for general jurisdiction).

一名居住在A州的原告在A州联邦法院对一家B州母公司及其一家外国子公司提起了非正常死亡诉讼。原告声称，该子公司在欧洲生产的轮胎导致其妻子在欧洲的一场车祸中死亡。

该母公司在美国各地（包括A州）都有大量业务。该子公司在A州没有开展任何业务，也没有员工或银行账户。该子公司为其欧洲市场生产轮胎，但其2%的轮胎由母公司在A州分销。该子公司已动议以缺乏属人管辖权为由驳回诉讼。

法院是否应批准该子公司的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为该子公司2%的轮胎通过商业流进入了A州。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为对母公司已确立了一般属人管辖权。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为事故并非发生在美国境内。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为该子公司与A州缺乏持续、系统且重大的联系。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：外国子公司在州内没有持续、系统、足够“在家”的联系时，法院能不能对它行使一般管辖权（general jurisdiction）。

三秒认题路径：

没在州内送达 → 也没同意 → 先看具体管辖 → 再看一般管辖 → 不能立刻管

核心法律规则

人身管辖权（personal jurisdiction）先看有没有送达诉状（service of process）或同意（consent）；这里都没有，所以要看最低接触。具体管辖权（specific jurisdiction）要求争议与被告在州内的最低接触有关，而且被告要有purposeful availment，考场意思：不能只是货物“碰巧”到了这个州。一般管辖权（general jurisdiction）则要求被告在该州有持续、系统、足够强的联系，强到几乎“at home”，考场意思：不是做点生意就算。

核心判例： Goodyear Dunlop Tires Operations, S.A. v. Brown — 一般管辖权要到“几乎在家”，外国母公司或子公司单靠零散销售通常不够。

思维导图

先问：州 A 法院对这个子公司有没有 人身管辖权（personal jurisdiction）？
1. 有无送达或同意？
题干没写州内送达，也没写合同同意 → 直接往下查最低接触
2. 具体管辖权（specific jurisdiction）？
看事故/主张是否“连着”州内接触。这里货物只有 2% 进入州 A，但子公司没有在州内经营、雇员、银行账户，也没有主动瞄准州 A。
只有“货进了州”不够；没有 purposeful targeting，就卡掉具体管辖权
3. 一般管辖权（general jurisdiction）？
要“持续、系统、足够强”的联系，强到几乎 at home。子公司在欧洲设立、也不在州 A 营业 → 不在家。
没有“在家”级别联系 → 也没有一般管辖权 → 结论：准许撤诉
答案落点： D 说的是“缺少持续、系统、实质性联系”，正中考点。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：2% of tires 都进了州 A，说明已经有联系了，应该能管。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是具体瞄准或在家级别的联系，不是货物有没有“碰到”这个州。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 无州内经营、雇员、账户，说明子公司没有持续、系统、足够“在家”的联系，所以州 A 不能对它行使一般管辖权。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 stream of commerce 当成自动成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 母公司代入误判

✕ B: 母公司的联系不能直接算到子公司头上。

❌ 事实误判 | 地点条件偷换

✕ C: 事故在欧洲，不代表美国法院就一定不能管。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分具体管辖和一般管辖，再盯“在家”与“主动瞄准”两个门槛。

考场速记

口诀：“货进州，不等于能管州；要么连着案子，要么强到在家。”

看到 general jurisdiction，先问一句：被告是不是已经“at home”？不是，就别被“有点销售”带跑。

B.text: general personal jurisdiction established over the parent corporation

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Two siblings inherited their $250,000 family home located in State A after their parents died in a car accident. The brother is 20 years old and lives in State A. The sister is 13 years old and now lives with her uncle, who has not yet been appointed her legal guardian. The brother wants to sell the home, while the uncle wants to use the home as a rental property.
The brother filed a lawsuit against his sister in a federal court in State A, requesting that the court order the sale of the home and split the proceeds between the children. The brother hired a process server, who hand-delivered a copy of the summons and complaint to the uncle at his apartment in State B.
A State A statute provides that process may be served on a minor by "leaving a copy of the summons and complaint with the minor's parent or legally appointed guardian." A State B statute allows service of process on a minor by "leaving a copy of the summons and complaint with the minor's parent or legally appointed guardian, an adult family member with whom the minor resides, or a married-minor's adult spouse."
The sister's lawyer filed a motion to dismiss the suit for insufficient service of process.
Will the court likely grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because the brother complied with the State B service-of-process statute.
choices.B: No, because the federal rules allow a family member to receive process on a minor's behalf.
choices.C: Yes, because minors cannot be sued in federal court.
choices.D: Yes, because the brother did not comply with the State A service-of-process statute.

questions.explanation:
Special service-of-process rules
Incompetent or minor Plaintiff must follow rules of state where service is made
Federal
government/agency		 Plaintiff must deliver summons & complaint to all of the following:
  • (1) U.S. attorney for district where action is brought or designated employee or (2) civil-process clerk at U.S. attorney's office via registered or certified mail
  • U.S. Attorney General via registered or certified mail AND
  • agency or officer whose conduct is challenged via registered or certified mail
Foreign government Plaintiff must deliver summons & complaint:
  • by special arrangement between plaintiff & foreign state
  • if no special arrangement, by international convention
  • if no convention, by sending to head of ministry of foreign affairs via mail requiring signed receipt OR
  • if no notice by mail within 30 days, by sending two copies to U.S. Secretary of State via mail requiring signed receipt
State or local
government		 Plaintiff must either:
  • deliver notice to chief executive officer OR
  • follow rules of state where government is located

A plaintiff must give a defendant notice of a lawsuit by properly serving the defendant with a summons and complaint (ie, service of process). Like all defendants located in the U.S. who are sued in federal court, a minor or legally incompetent defendant must be served within 90 days after the complaint is filed. But under FRCP 4(g), a minor or legally incompetent defendant must be served in accordance with the service-of-process rules of the state where service is made. Here, those are the rules of State B.

State B allows a minor to be served by leaving process with "an adult family member with whom the minor resides." Here, the brother's process server hand-delivered the summons and complaint to the uncle at his apartment in State B. And since the 13-year-old sister resides with that uncle, service of process was sufficient. Therefore, the court will likely deny the sister's motion to dismiss.

(Choice B) A family member can receive process on a minor's behalf only if the state where service is made allows such service of process—eg, here, allowed in State B but not State A.

(Choice C) Minors can be sued in federal court—as anticipated by FRCP 4's provision for serving a minor.

(Choice D) A minor must be served with process pursuant to the service-of-process rules of the state where service is made (State B)—not the state where the suit is filed (State A).

📌 Educational Objective

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 4(g), a minor or legally incompetent defendant can only be served with process by following the service rules of the state where service is made.

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(g) (service on minor or incompetent person).

一对兄妹在父母因车祸去世后，继承了他们位于A州的价值25万美元的家庭住宅。哥哥20岁，居住在A州。妹妹13岁，现与其叔叔同住，其叔叔尚未被指定为她的法定监护人。哥哥想出售该住宅，而叔叔则想将该住宅用作出租物业。

哥哥在A州的联邦法院对妹妹提起了诉讼，请求法院命令出售该住宅，并将收益在兄妹之间分配。哥哥聘请了一名送达员，该送达员在B州的叔叔公寓里，将传票和诉状的副本亲手交给了叔叔。

A州的一项法规规定，可以通过“将传票和诉状的副本留置于未成年人的父母或法定监护人处”的方式向未成年人送达诉讼文书。B州的一项法规允许通过“将传票和诉状的副本留置于未成年人的父母或法定监护人、与未成年人同住的成年家庭成员，或已婚未成年人的成年配偶处”的方式向未成年人送达诉讼文书。

妹妹的律师以诉讼文书送达不充分为由，提起了驳回诉讼的动议。

法院是否可能批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为哥哥遵守了B州的诉讼文书送达法规。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为联邦规则允许家庭成员代表未成年人接收诉讼文书。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为未成年人不能在联邦法院被起诉。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为哥哥没有遵守A州的诉讼文书送达法规。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Service of process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：未成年人（minor）在联邦法院里怎么送达，关键看送达地所在州（state where service is made）的规则，不是起诉州的规则。

三秒认题路径：

minor被告 → 联邦送达 → 看送达地州法 → State B规则 → 送达有效

核心法律规则

在联邦民事诉讼里，给未成年人（minor）送达传票和起诉状时，FRCP 4(g)要求你按送达发生地所在州的送达规则来做，考场意思：不是看案件在哪个州立案，而是看你把文件递到哪个州。成人家庭成员（adult family member）如果是该州规则允许的接收对象，送达就可能有效。这里先不用纠结家事背景，先抓送达地规则。

核心判例： 本题直接锁定 FRCP 4(g) 的送达规则；考场上记住：未成年人送达看的是送达地州法，不是起诉州法。

思维导图

先问：这是不是终局判决（final judgment）问题？
NO本题不是上诉可受理性，而是服务是否有效（service of process）。
再看：被送达人是minor，规则要转向哪儿？
看送达地按state where service is made的规则走。
卡死点：State B 允许把文件交给与未成年人同住的成人家庭成员。
事实命中传票和起诉状交给了住在 State B 的叔叔，而姐姐和叔叔同住。
结论：送达有效 → 答案 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 State A 也有自己的送达法，就应该回头看起诉州的规则。

但考试真正问的是：FRCP 4(g)把你锁到送达发生地，所以本题只看 State B。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 把起诉状交给 State B 的叔叔，而 State B 允许“与未成年人同住的成人家庭成员”接收送达，所以送达有效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 家属代收误判

✕ B: 把family member当成联邦统一规则了。

❌ 法律适用 | 诉讼主体误判

✕ C: 看到未成年人就误以为不能被起诉。

❌ 事实误判 | 起诉州偷换

✕ D: 把State A当成送达判断标准了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁被告类型，再把规则切到“送达发生地”，最后对照州法是否允许代收。

考场速记

记忆口诀：minor / incompetent 的送达，先问“where service is made”。本题一句话记住：送达地州法管代收，起诉州法不抢答。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
After 10 years of marriage, a husband and wife decided to separate. The husband remained in the family home in State A, while the wife moved into an apartment in State B.
Seven months later, the wife filed for divorce in a state court in State B. She knew that her husband would be attending a professional conference in State B the following week, so she hired a process server to personally hand-deliver a copy of the divorce petition and the State B summons to him at the conference.
The husband moved to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.
Should the court grant the husband's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because the husband was personally served with process in State B.
choices.B: No, because there is no other state that is more convenient for both of the parties than State B.
choices.C: Yes, because State A was the couple's home state for 10 years.
choices.D: Yes, because the husband was in State B for a matter unrelated to the marriage.

questions.explanation:
Personal jurisdiction
(court's authority over defendant)
Type Requirements
Service of
process		 • Serving process on defendant voluntarily in state where court is located (ie, forum state)
Consent • Express – contractual agreement (eg, forum-selection clause)
• Implied – engaging in specific activity that state has substantial interest in regulating (eg, driving on public roads)
• Waiver – untimely objection to personal jurisdiction
• Appearance – voluntarily appearing in court to litigate merits of case
Specific
(case-linked)		 • Plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to defendant's minimum contacts (ie, purposeful availment) with forum state AND
• Exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play & substantial justice
General
(all-purpose)		 • Defendant has continuous & systematic contacts with forum state so substantial that defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, defendant's domicile)

Due process requires that a court have personal jurisdiction over all of the parties in a dispute before it. One way to establish personal jurisdiction is through tag jurisdiction (ie, transient jurisdiction). Under this method, personal jurisdiction is acquired by serving the defendant* with formal process while the defendant is voluntarily in the forum state—even if briefly and for a purpose unrelated to the plaintiff's claim.

Here, the husband was served with the divorce petition and State B summons while he was in State B for a conference—a matter unrelated to the marriage (Choice D). Therefore, the court has personal jurisdiction over the husband and should deny his motion to dismiss.

*Personal jurisdiction is always focused on the defendant because the plaintiff consents to personal jurisdiction by filing the suit in that court.

(Choice B) Whether another state or court is a more convenient forum for the parties is only considered when a change of venue is requested.

(Choice C) Although State A was the couple's home state for 10 years, State B has personal jurisdiction since the wife initiated the suit there and the husband was served with process there.

📌 Educational Objective

Personal jurisdiction can be established by serving the defendant with formal process while the defendant is voluntarily in the forum state even if briefly and for a purpose unrelated to the plaintiff's claim.

📚 References
  • Burnham v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 495 U.S. 604, 619 (1990) (holding that personal jurisdiction is established when the defendant is served with process in the forum state).

结婚10年后，一对夫妻决定分居。丈夫留在A州的婚房内，而妻子则搬到了B州的一间公寓里。

七个月后，妻子向B州的州法院提起了离婚诉讼。她知道丈夫下周将在B州参加一个专业会议，因此她聘请了一名送达员，在会议上亲自将离婚申请书副本和B州的传票送达给丈夫。

丈夫以缺乏对人管辖权为由，请求驳回此案。

法院是否应批准丈夫的驳回请求？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为丈夫在B州被当面送达了诉讼文书。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为对双方而言，没有比B州更方便的州了。
zh-choices.C: 应该，因为A州是这对夫妻生活了10年的家庭所在州。
zh-choices.D: 应该，因为丈夫身在B州是为了一件与婚姻无关的事宜。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - In personam jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告人在论坛州被正式送达（tag jurisdiction / transient jurisdiction）时，法院能不能直接取得对他的人身管辖权。

三秒认题路径：

州内送达 → 论坛州 → 临时在场 → 直接管辖 → 不能驳回

核心法律规则

拿分规则

人身管辖权（personal jurisdiction）先看被告，不看原告讲不讲理。临时管辖（tag jurisdiction）的考场意思：被告只要在论坛州（forum state）里，且被正式送达诉讼文书（formal process），法院通常就能管，不管他来这里是不是为了这起案子。

所以，这题里丈夫在 State B 开会时被亲自送达离婚传票和起诉状，已经踩中 tag jurisdiction，州 B 法院就有对他的人身管辖权，不能因为他“只是路过”就驳回。

核心判例： Burnham v. Superior Court of California — 被告在论坛州内被送达，通常就足够建立人身管辖权。

思维导图

先问：有没有终局判决？
有→ 走普通上诉。
没有→ 继续看是否有例外。
这题的关键例外：州内送达能否直接建立管辖？
被告在 State B voluntarily in the forum state，又被正式送达离婚传票。
卡死点：不管争议和婚姻有没有关系，tag jurisdiction 仍然成立。
结果：法院对丈夫有人身管辖权 → 答案选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：夫妻长期住在 State A，或者丈夫去 State B 只是出差，法院就不能管他。

但考试真正问的是：他有没有在论坛州内被正式送达；一旦有，tag jurisdiction 就能直接成立。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的路过有没有意义」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 personal service in State B 直接触发 tag jurisdiction，所以州 B 法院可以管丈夫，不能准许驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 管辖救济混同

✕ B: 把 more convenient 当成人身管辖标准了。

❌ 事实误判 | 主页州误读

✕ C: 盯着 State A 的婚姻历史，却漏掉了 State B 内的送达这个关键事实。

❌ 法律适用 | 目的相关误套

✕ D: 以为出差目的不相关就没管辖，但 unrelated 在 tag jurisdiction 里不重要。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否在论坛州内被正式送达；只要命中，就别再纠结婚姻背景或方便与否。

考场速记

记忆口诀：州内送达，先管再说。 只要被告在论坛州里被正式送达，通常就有 人身管辖权（personal jurisdiction）。

Burnham 记一遍：服务在场，管辖到场。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
The owner of a parcel of land in State A, the owner's state of residence, entered into a contract with a company to construct a residence on the land. The contract called for any dispute arising from the contract to be brought in a state court in State A. When a contract dispute did arise, the owner filed a breach-of-contract action in federal court in State B, where the company was incorporated. The company has challenged the venue of the court.
Of the following, which option is most likely to be available to the court?

choices.A: Dismissal of the action for improper venue.
choices.B: Dismissal of the action under the doctrine of forum non conveniens.
choices.C: Remand of the action to a state court in State A.
choices.D: Transfer of the action to a state court in State A.

questions.explanation:
Doctrine of forum non conveniens
Definition
  • Power of federal court to dismiss or stay lawsuit when state or foreign judicial system is better suited to hear case
Private interest
factors
  • Accessibility of evidence
  • Availability of witnesses
  • Burden on defendant
  • Enforceability of judgment
Public interest
factors
  • Ability to comprehend substantive law
  • Choice of law
  • Interest of jury/community
  • Functionality of foreign judicial system

The appropriate way for a federal court to enforce a forum-selection clause that designates a state or foreign forum is to dismiss the action under the doctrine of forum non conveniens. This is a common-law doctrine that allows a court to dismiss an action if the court finds that the forum would be too inconvenient for parties and witnesses and that a more convenient venue is available.

Here, the owner filed suit against the company in federal court in State B for breach of contract. But the contract contained a forum-selection clause that called for any dispute arising from the contract to be brought in a state court in State A. And since the forum-selection clause designates a state forum, dismissal of the action under the doctrine of forum non conveniens is the option most likely to be available to the court.

(Choice A) Venue is proper in the State B federal court because the company was incorporated—and therefore resides—in State B. However, most federal courts will enforce the parties' forum selection clause even if venue is proper in the court where suit was filed.

(Choice B) The appropriate way for a federal court to enforce a forum-selection clause that designates a state or foreign forum is to dismiss the action under the doctrine of forum non conveniens.

(Choice C) The State B federal court cannot remand the case to the State A state court because the case had not been removed from the state court or originally brought in that court.

(Choice D) A federal court may transfer an action to another federal court—but not to a state court.

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court may dismiss an action under the doctrine of forum non conveniens to enforce a forum-selection clause that designates a state court as the proper forum.

📚 References
  • Atlantic Marine Constr. Co. v. United States Dist. Ct. for the W. Dist. of Tex., 571 U.S. 49, 60 (2013) (noting that forum non conveniens is the proper means of enforcing a forum-selection clause that specifies a state court).

在以下选项中，该法院最有可能采取哪种选择？

zh-choices.A: 以审判地不当（improper venue）为由驳回诉讼。
zh-choices.B: 根据不方便法院原则（doctrine of forum non conveniens）驳回诉讼。
zh-choices.C: 将诉讼发回（remand）至A州的州法院。
zh-choices.D: 将诉讼移送（transfer）至A州的州法院。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Venue, forum non conveniens, transfer

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：forum-selection clause（论坛选择条款）指定州法院时，联邦法院要不要用forum non conveniens（不方便法院原则）直接驳回，而不是转去州法院。

三秒认题路径：

州法院条款 → 联邦起诉 → 不能转州院 → 看 FNC → 选 B

核心法律规则

forum non conveniens（不方便法院原则）：考场意思是，联邦法院觉得另一个法院更合适时，可以dismiss（驳回）或暂缓，而不是硬审到底。

若合同里的forum-selection clause（论坛选择条款）指定的是state court（州法院）或外国法院，联邦法院通常用这个原则来执行条款。transfer（移送）只能在联邦法院之间玩，不能移到州法院。

所以这题里，条款写明去State A州法院，联邦法院最可能的动作就是直接dismiss（驳回），让当事人去州法院起诉。

核心判例： Atlantic Marine Constr. Co. v. U.S. Dist. Ct. — 论坛选择条款指向州法院时，联邦法院用 forum non conveniens 来执行。

思维导图

先看条款把案件送去哪里？
Yes：州法院 / 外国法院
联邦法院不走 transfer
→
用 forum non conveniens（不方便法院原则） 驳回
→
答：B
No：只是另一个联邦法院
可以考虑 transfer（移送）
本题事实
条款写的是 State A state court
→
所以不是 venue 问题优先，而是执行条款的问题

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告在State B注册成立，所以这里venue 好像也没问题。

但考试真正问的是：联邦法院怎么执行“必须去State A州法院”的条款，不是先比谁住哪儿。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 forum-selection clause 明写去 State A 州法院，联邦法院最合适的动作就是用 forum non conveniens 驳回。

❌ 事实误判 | 管辖事实偷换

✕ A: 只盯着 corporated in State B，忘了条款才是关键。

❌ 法律适用 | 反向救济误用

✕ C: 想把案子“发回”州院，但这里根本不是撤回后的 remand 场景。

❌ 概念混淆 | 移送对象张冠李戴

✕ D: 以为 transfer 能把案子送到州法院，其实只能在联邦法院之间移送。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓条款指定的论坛，再判断联邦法院是移送还是直接按 forum non conveniens 驳回。

考场速记

口诀：条款指向州法院或外国法院，联邦法院通常走 forum non conveniens；指向另一家联邦法院，才想到 transfer。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A driver from State A was texting and driving when she hit a pedestrian from State B in a crosswalk in State B. The pedestrian suffered multiple injuries and sued the driver for gross negligence in a federal district court in State B. In his complaint, the pedestrian sought compensatory damages of $75,000 for lost wages and medical expenses, $10,000 for attorney's fees, and $100,000 for punitive damages.
At the conclusion of trial, the jury awarded the pedestrian $35,000 for lost wages and medical expenses and $30,000 for punitive damages. The driver immediately moved to dismiss the case, arguing that the amount in controversy was insufficient to establish subject-matter jurisdiction.
State B permits the recovery of punitive damages but not attorney's fees in a gross negligence action.
Should the court grant the driver's motion?

choices.A: No, because the total amount in controversy was $185,000.
choices.B: No, because the total amount in controversy was $175,000.
choices.C: Yes, because the total amount in controversy was $75,000.
choices.D: Yes, because the total amount in controversy was $65,000.

questions.explanation:
Calculating amount in controversy
Compensatory damages
(always included)
Punitive damages (if permitted by law)
Attorney’s fees (if permitted by law or contract)
— $75,000 in controversy
Interest & costs (never included)

Subject-matter jurisdiction is established when a case satisfies either federal-question jurisdiction (not seen here) or diversity jurisdiction. Diversity jurisdiction exists when the opposing parties are completely diverse—eg, the plaintiff and defendant are citizens of different states—and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

The amount in controversy is determined at the time the plaintiff files the complaint and includes all amounts asserted in good faith except interest, costs, and damages that are not legally recoverable. As a result, the following sums may be included in the amount in controversy:

  • Compensatory damages – money sought to compensate the plaintiff for his/her actual loss or harm (eg, pain and suffering, lost wages) that is always included in the amount in controversy
  • Punitive damages – money sought to punish and deter outrageous, malicious, and evil conduct that is included if permitted by state law
  • Attorney's fees – amount billed to a client for legal services provided that is included if permitted by state law or contract

Here, the complaint requested $75,000 in compensatory damages, $100,000 in punitive damages, and $10,000 in attorney's fees. State B permits the recovery of punitive damages but not attorney's fees in this gross negligence action, so the amount in controversy was $175,000 ($75,000 + $100,000). Therefore, the amount-in-controversy requirement was met and the driver's motion should be denied (Choices A & C).

(Choice D) The fact that the jury awarded the pedestrian only $65,000 is irrelevant in calculating the amount in controversy. The reason is that this amount is determined at the time the complaint is filed—not by later events.

📌 Educational Objective

Diversity jurisdiction exists when the opposing parties are completely diverse and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000. The amount in controversy always includes compensatory damages and includes punitive damages (if permitted by state law) and attorney's fees (if permitted by state law or contract).

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 952 (2020) (explaining that punitive damages are included in the amount in controversy if permitted by law).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 960 (2020) (describing that attorney's fees are included in the amount in controversy if permitted by law or contract).
questions.zh-question:
一名来自A州的司机在B州的一处人行横道上边开车边发短信，撞上了一名来自B州的行人。该行人身受多处伤害，遂以重大过失为由，在B州的联邦地区法院对该司机提起诉讼。行人在其诉状中，请求赔偿因工资损失和医疗费用产生的补偿性损害赔偿金75,000美元，律师费10,000美元，以及惩罚性损害赔偿金100,000美元。

审判结束时，陪审团裁决赔偿该行人因工资损失和医疗费用产生的补偿性损害赔偿金35,000美元，以及惩罚性损害赔偿金30,000美元。司机立即动议驳回此案，主张争议金额不足以确立事物管辖权。

B州法律允许在重大过失诉讼中获赔惩罚性损害赔偿金，但不允许获赔律师费。

法院是否应批准该司机的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为争议总金额为185,000美元。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为争议总金额为175,000美元。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为争议总金额为75,000美元。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为争议总金额为65,000美元。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Diversity jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多元管辖里的 争议金额（amount in controversy） 要按起诉时算，且可把合法的补偿性损害赔偿、惩罚性赔偿算进去，但不能把不允许的律师费和后来陪审团少判的金额拿来反向推翻管辖。

三秒认题路径：

多元管辖 → 争议金额 → 起诉时算 → 算赔偿项 → 够 75k

核心法律规则

多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction） 先看双方是否完全不同州，然后看 争议金额（amount in controversy） 是否超过 75,000 美元。考场意思：这里不是看最后判了多少，而是看起诉时原告善意主张了多少。补偿性损害赔偿（compensatory damages） 一定算；惩罚性损害赔偿（punitive damages） 只要州法允许就能算；律师费（attorney's fees） 只有州法或合同允许时才算。

核心判例： 28 U.S.C. § 1332 的规则配合联邦法院常规：争议金额按起诉时的善意请求判断，不因后来陪审团少判而回头把管辖打掉。

思维导图

1. 先看双方国籍
原告是 State B，司机是 State A；完全多元 这一关过了。
2. 起诉时主张金额
看 complaint 写了什么，不看庭审后陪审团改判多少。
3. 先算能算的
补偿性 75,000 + 惩罚性 100,000 = 175,000。
4. 别把不能算的塞进去
律师费不算，因为 State B 在这类 gross negligence 里不允许。
5. 结论门槛
超过 75,000 就有管辖；这里明显超过，所以 不能驳回。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：陪审团最后只判了 65,000，所以联邦法院就没管辖了。

但考试真正问的是：争议金额 该按起诉时的善意请求算，不按事后结果倒推。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干请求的 75,000 补偿性损害赔偿 加上 100,000 惩罚性损害赔偿，已达 175,000；State B 又允许这类 punitive damages，所以管辖成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 compensatory 和 punitive 都算对了，却硬把律师费也塞进去。

❌ 法律适用 | 起诉时点误判

✕ C: 只盯着 $75,000，忽略惩罚性赔偿也能计入。

❌ 事实误判 | 事后金额偷换

✕ D: 拿 $65,000 的陪审团结果回头改写起诉时的争议金额。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先锁定起诉时金额，再检查哪些赔偿项目能合法计入。

考场速记

记住一句：争议金额（amount in controversy） 先看起诉时的善意请求，补偿性永远算，惩罚性和律师费只在州法或合同允许时算；事后少判，不会把已经成立的多元管辖倒推没。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A man domiciled in State A sued a corporation in a federal court in State A for violating a federal law that prohibits collaboration with terror organizations. The man alleged that the corporation's South American subsidiary provided funds to a notorious terror group that carried out an attack in South America, resulting in the deaths of the man's parents. The man claims that the corporation is vicariously liable for the subsidiary's actions.
The corporation is incorporated and has its headquarters in Europe. The corporation also has a United States subsidiary that maintains an office in State A.
The corporation has moved to dismiss the lawsuit for lack of personal jurisdiction.
How will the court likely rule on the corporation's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because general jurisdiction exists in State A.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because specific jurisdiction exists in State A.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because foreign corporations are never subject to personal jurisdiction in the United States.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because neither specific nor general jurisdiction exists in State A.

14. Forum selection clause:

Courts must have personal jurisdiction over the parties to satisfy the constitutional guarantee of due process. Personal jurisdiction can be established through a defendant's consent or by serving process while the defendant is physically present in the state where the court is located (ie, the forum state)—not seen here. Personal jurisdiction can also be established through:

  • specific jurisdiction – when the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state such that the exercise of jurisdiction would not offend notions of fair play and substantial justice or
  • general jurisdiction – when the defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" there (ie, the defendant's domicile).

A corporation is domiciled in the state where it is incorporated and where it maintains its principal place of business (eg, its headquarters). However, the location and activities of a corporation's subsidiary have no effect on its domicile.

Here, the State A federal court lacks specific jurisdiction since the claim arises from and is closely related to the corporation's contacts with South America—where its subsidiary allegedly funded the terror group and the attack occurred (Choice B). The State A federal court also lacks general jurisdiction because the corporation is domiciled in Europe—where it is incorporated and maintains its headquarters (Choice A). Therefore, the court will likely grant the corporation's motion to dismiss.

(Choice C) Foreign corporations can be subject to personal jurisdiction in the United States—eg, through consent or minimum contacts.

📌 Educational Objective

General jurisdiction exists when a defendant has continuous and systematic contacts with the forum state that are so substantial that the defendant is essentially "at home" there. A corporation is at home (ie, domiciled) in the state where it is incorporated and maintains its principal place of business—not where its subsidiary has an office.

📚 References
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the requirements for specific jurisdiction).
  • Daimler AG v. Bauman, 571 U.S. 117, 138–39 (2014) (holding that a subsidiary's activities do not subject a parent corporation to general jurisdiction).

该公司在欧洲注册成立，总部也设在欧洲。该公司还有一个美国子公司，在A州设有一个办事处。

该公司已因缺乏对人管辖权为由，提出驳回诉讼的动议。

法院将可能如何裁定该公司的驳回动议？

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：母公司在州内没有足够联系时，能不能因为子公司在该州有办公室，就被判定有一般管辖权（general jurisdiction）或特定管辖权（specific jurisdiction）。

三秒认题路径：

先看州内联系 → 再分两种管辖 → 子公司不能自动算 → 母公司“在家”吗 → 不能上诉式幻想

核心法律规则

个人管辖权（personal jurisdiction）的入口是被告要么同意，要么有足够的州内联系；没有这些，法院就不能让它进场应诉。特定管辖权（specific jurisdiction）要求诉因和被告在论坛州的最低联系（minimum contacts）有直接关系，所以本题里侵权和资金流向都发生在南美，不是州A。一般管辖权（general jurisdiction）只看被告是否“在家”，公司通常只在注册地（state of incorporation）和主要营业地（principal place of business）“在家”，不是子公司有办公室就够了。

核心判例： Daimler AG v. Bauman — 子公司的活动不会把母公司自动拉进一般管辖权；Bristol-Myers Squibb — 诉因必须和论坛州联系真正挂钩。

思维导图

先问：State A 能不能管到这家公司？
第一关：有没有终局判决（final judgment）问题？——本题不是上诉题，直接进管辖分析。
第二关：看特定管辖权（specific jurisdiction）
诉因要来自或紧密关联被告在州内的联系。
卡死点：案子发生在南美，关联的是南美子公司，不是 State A。
第三关：看一般管辖权（general jurisdiction）
公司要“在家”，通常是注册地 + 主要营业地。
卡死点：母公司在欧洲注册、总部也在欧洲；州A只有子公司办公室，不能算“在家”。
结论：两条路都断掉 → 只能D 诉讼驳回。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：State A 里有美国子公司办公室，所以母公司应该能被拉进来。
但考试真正问的是：母公司自己有没有足够联系，或者诉因有没有直接连到它在州内的行为。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题最容易被“子公司在州内”带偏，但题干只给了母公司在欧洲注册和总部在欧洲，州A联系不够，不能把子公司办公室当成母公司“在家”的证据。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只给了 South American subsidiary 和州A里的子公司办公室，没有给母公司在州A的最低联系或“在家”基础，所以两种管辖都不成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 总部当州内

✕ A: 把 office 直接当成母公司“在家”，把子公司活动混成母公司联系。

❌ 事实误判 | 南美联系偷换

✕ B: 以为南美事故能自动撑起州A的 minimum contacts，其实联系不在论坛州。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对化错误

✕ C: 看到“外国公司”就想全盘排除，但它仍可能因同意或联系受管辖。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分特定与一般管辖，再把子公司联系和母公司联系彻底拆开看。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“在家看注册地和总部，诉因看州内联系；子公司有办公室，不等于母公司有管辖。”

这题不用被故事吓住，直接抓两句：specific jurisdiction 看案子和州内行为，general jurisdiction 看公司是否“在家”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A computer company, incorporated in State A and with its principal place of business in State B, manufactured a laptop that would overheat if left on for over 24 hours. A college student purchased this laptop in State B, where she resided. While at her apartment, the student left the laptop on for over 24 hours. The laptop exploded, causing her to sustain severe injuries.
After recuperating from her injuries, the student moved to State C and sued the computer company in State C federal court to recover $200,000 for her injuries.
The computer company filed a motion to transfer the lawsuit to the State B federal court on the ground that State C is an improper venue.
How will the State C federal court likely rule on the computer company's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the court only has the power to dismiss the student's lawsuit.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because venue is proper in State C.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the doctrine of forum non conveniens allows for such a transfer.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because venue is improper in State C.

questions.explanation:
Venue
Proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1391) 		Case may be brought in any federal district where:
  • any defendant resides, if defendants all reside in same state
  • substantial part of events giving rise to claim occurred or property at issue is located
  • any defendant is subject to court's personal jurisdiction (if neither of the above provisions applies)
Transfer from proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1404) 		When venue is proper, district court may transfer case to any other proper venue for convenience of parties/witnesses & in interest of justice
Transfer or dismissal from improper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1406) 		When venue is improper, district court must either:
  • dismiss case
  • transfer case to proper venue (if interest of justice requires)

Venue—ie, the geographic location of the specific federal district in which suit may be brought—is proper in any federal district where:

  • any defendant resides—eg, where a company is incorporated or maintains its principal place of business—so long as all the defendants reside in the same state
  • a substantial part of the events that gave rise to the suit occurred or the property at issue is located or
  • any defendant is subject to the court's personal jurisdiction (if neither of the above provisions applies).

Here, the computer company resides in State A (state of incorporation) and State B (principal place of business)—not State C. And the events giving rise to the suit—the computer purchase and the explosion—occurred only in State B. Therefore, venue is improper in State C (Choice B).

When venue is improper, the federal court must either (1) dismiss the lawsuit or (2) transfer it to a federal court with proper venue (Choice A). Federal courts prefer transfer over dismissal for judicial efficiency. Therefore, the State C federal court will likely grant the computer company's motion to transfer the student's lawsuit to the State B federal court—where venue is proper.

(Choice C) The doctrine of forum non conveniens allows a federal court to dismiss or stay a lawsuit—even when venue is proper in that court—if a state or foreign judicial system is better suited to hear the dispute (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court with improper venue must either transfer the suit to a federal court with proper venue (preferred) or dismiss the case.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1391 (venue).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1406 (transfer when venue is improper).

电脑公司提出动议，请求以C州为不适格审判地为由，将诉讼移送至B州联邦法院。

C州联邦法院可能会如何裁定电脑公司的该项动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为法院仅有权驳回该学生的诉讼。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为C州是适格的审判地。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为不方便法院原则(forum non conveniens)允许此类移送。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Change of venue

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：先判断 venue（审理地点） 在 State C 是否本来就对，再决定法院是该 transfer（移送） 还是 dismiss（驳回）。

三秒认题路径：

先看 venue → 再看 §1391 → 不对就 §1406 → 可移送 → 选 D

核心法律规则

Proper venue（适格审理地点） 的考场意思：先问这个联邦法院能不能“放这案子”，不是先问案子谁对谁错。公司被告的 venue 通常看它的居住地，也就是公司成立州和主要营业地州；还可以看 substantial part of events（主要事件发生地）。

如果 State C 既不是公司居住地，也不是事故关键事件发生地，venue is improper（地点不当）。这时法院走 28 U.S.C. § 1406：要么 dismiss，要么为司法效率 transfer 到正确的联邦法院。

核心规则： Forum non conveniens 是“地点本来就对，但别的法域更合适”才用；本题是 venue 根本不对，所以不能拿它来支持移送。

思维导图

先问：State C 的 venue 本来就对吗？
NO 公司不住 State C；公司只在 State A（成立）和 State B（主要营业地）“居住”。
NO 事故关键事件也不在 State C；购买和爆炸都发生在 State B。
第三关卡死：State C venue 不当 → 不能用 forum non conveniens 来补救。
下一步 venue 不当时，法院按 § 1406 处理：优先 transfer 到正确 venue。
结论：State C 法院会批准移送到 State B → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 State C 不是最方便的地方，那就用 forum non conveniens 把案子移走。

但考试真正问的是：先看这个法院的 venue 对不对；如果 venue 本来就不对，走的是 § 1406，不是 forum non conveniens。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 State C 既非公司居住地，也非事件发生地，所以 venue 不当；法院可依 § 1406 把案子移送到 State B。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只会驳回

✕ A: 误以为 venue 不当只能 dismiss the lawsuit，但 § 1406 也允许移送。

❌ 事实误判 | 把州 C 当事件地

✕ B: 把 State C 当成事件发生地了，但购买和爆炸都在 State B。

❌ 法律适用 | 混用不便法院

✕ C: 把 forum non conveniens 搬来套错题；它不是 venue 不当时的移送理由。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先按 §1391 查 venue，再决定是 §1406 移送还是驳回。

考场速记

记住一句：venue 先判对不对，错了就看 § 1406；想移到别处，优先 transfer，不要先想到 forum non conveniens。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A limited liability company and a corporation entered into a contract in which the corporation agreed to deliver 100 tons of refined ore to the limited liability company in State A. The company maintains its principal place of business in State A. It has two members: one lives in State A and the other lives in State B. The corporation is both incorporated and keeps its principal place of business in State B. The corporation frequently conducts business in State A and keeps a refinery there to service its State A customers.
After the corporation failed to deliver 100 tons of refined ore, the company sued the corporation for breach of contract in a federal court in State A, seeking $1 million in damages. Sixty-one days after the company filed suit, a professional process server personally served the summons and complaint on the corporation's chief operating officer while she was touring the refinery, and copies of the summons and complaint were mailed to the corporation. Upon receiving service of process, the corporation moved to dismiss the lawsuit.
If the court grants the motion, which is the most likely reason?

choices.A: Improper venue, because the corporation's principal place of business is in State B.
choices.B: Lack of personal jurisdiction, because the corporation is domiciled in State B.
choices.C: Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, because the opposing parties are not diverse.
choices.D: Untimely service of process, because the summons and complaint were served more than 60 days after the complaint was filed.

questions.explanation:
Citizenship for diversity jurisdiction

Individual

State of domicile

Corporation

State of
incorporation
Principal place
of business

Unincorporated association

Every state where members are domiciled

A lawsuit should be dismissed if the court lacks subject-matter jurisdiction—ie, the authority to hear a particular type of case. This breach-of-contract case does not present a federal question, so subject-matter jurisdiction must be established through diversity jurisdiction. Diversity jurisdiction exists when the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states. A party's citizenship is determined as follows:

  • Individual – the state where the individual resides and intends to remain indefinitely (ie, state of domicile)
  • Corporation – the state(s) where it is incorporated and/or has its principal place of business
  • Unincorporated association (eg, partnership, limited liability company) – every state where its partners or members are domiciled

Here, the corporation is a citizen of State B, where it is incorporated and has its principal place of business. The limited liability company is a citizen of State A and State B, where its two members are domiciled. Since both parties are citizens of State B, there is no diversity of citizenship. Therefore, the motion to dismiss was likely granted on this basis.

(Choice A) Venue is proper in the federal district where a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claim occurred—eg, where a contract was to be performed. Therefore, venue is proper in State A, where the ore was to be delivered.

(Choice B) A federal court acquires personal jurisdiction over an out-of-state corporation when a corporate officer (here, the chief operating officer) is served with process while voluntarily in the state where the court sits. Therefore, the State A court has personal jurisdiction over the State B corporation.

(Choice D) Service of process is timely if the summons and complaint are served within 90 days after the complaint is filed. Therefore, process was timely served 61 days after the complaint was filed.

📌 Educational Objective

Individuals are only citizens of their state of domicile. In contrast, corporations are citizens of the state(s) where they are incorporated and/or have their principal place of business, and unincorporated associations are citizens of every state where their members are domiciled.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).

MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Subject-matter jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦法院能不能靠多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction）立案，关键看双方当事人是否真的是不同州公民。

三秒认题路径：

合同纠纷 → 无联邦问题 → 看多元管辖 → LLC看成员籍贯 → 有同州公民 → 不能立案

核心法律规则

Subject-matter jurisdiction考场意思：法院有没有资格听这类案子，不是看被告态度好不好。这个案子是合同纠纷，没有联邦问题，所以只能靠diversity jurisdiction。

Diversity jurisdiction考场意思：争议金额超过 $75,000，而且原被告必须是不同州公民。公司（corporation）看incorporation和principal place of business；LLC要看每个成员的居住州/住所州。

这题里，公司是 State B 公民；LLC 既是 State A 公民，也是 State B 公民，所以双方在 State B 重叠，complete diversity 失败。

核心判例： 这里不用靠复杂判例，直接套多元管辖的民事规则：LLC 按成员籍贯算，公司按注册地和主营业地算，所以同州重叠就没管辖权。

思维导图

先问：联邦法院有没有 subject-matter jurisdiction？
YES 路：有联邦问题吗？——没有，因为只是违约合同。
NO 路：那就只能看 diversity jurisdiction。
第一关：$75,000 以上？——题干给了 $1 million，过关。
第二关：双方是否不同州公民？
LLC 公民 = 成员州籍；这里成员在 State A 和 State B。
公司公民：State B（注册地 + 主营业地都在 B）。
卡死结论：双方都在 State B 出现 → no complete diversity → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司在 State A 有很多业务、还有炼厂，所以应该能在 State A 被告。

但考试真正问的是：联邦法院有没有 subject-matter jurisdiction，不是州法院能不能管、也不是被告在州里活动多不多。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 LLC 的成员包含 State B，而公司本身也是 State B 公民，所以双方不满足 complete diversity，联邦法院最可能因无管辖权而驳回。

❌ 事实误判 | 主营业地偷换

✕ A: 把 principal place 当成 venue 结论，错把地点便利当成管辖权。

❌ 概念混淆 | 住所规则乱套

✕ B: 公司不是按“住哪儿”算公民，domiciled in State B 这句是把法人和自然人混了。

❌ 法律适用 | 90天规则错搬

✕ D: more than 60 days 不是本题标准；而且题目问的是驳回理由，不是送达细节。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否有联邦问题，再用“公司看注册地/主营业地，LLC看成员籍贯”秒杀多元管辖。

考场速记

记住一句：公司看两地，LLC看成员；只要同州重叠，多元管辖就断了。 这类题先别追着 venue 和送达跑，先卡 subject-matter jurisdiction。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A company incorporated and with its principal place of business in State A sued a partnership located in State B in a State A federal court to recover $30,000 for a breach of contract claim and $60,000 for a misrepresentation claim.
After the partnership filed an answer denying liability, the partnership's attorney learned that one of the partners had permanently moved to State A before the company filed its complaint. The attorney moved to dismiss the suit for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
How should the court rule on the motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the company and the partnership are diverse and the amount in controversy is satisfied.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the partnership waived its subject-matter jurisdiction defense by failing to include it in its answer.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because neither of the company's claims independently exceeds $75,000.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the company and the partnership are not diverse.

questions.explanation:
Citizenship for diversity jurisdiction
Person Citizen of state where domiciled—ie, physically present with intent to remain indefinitely
Corporation Citizen of every state where it (1) has been incorporated and/or (2) has its principal place of business
Unincorporated association Citizen of every state where its members are domiciled

A federal court can only hear a suit over which it has subject-matter jurisdiction—ie, authority to hear a particular type of case or controversy. The burden is on the party seeking to invoke the court's subject-matter jurisdiction (ie, the claimant) to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the court has either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – the claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not seen here) or
  • diversity jurisdiction – the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states (ie, are diverse) at the time the complaint is filed.

A corporation (eg, the company) is a citizen of every state where it is incorporated and/or has its principal place of business (here, State A). In contrast, an unincorporated association (eg, the partnership) is a citizen of every state where its members are domiciled—ie, where they reside and intend to remain indefinitely. Since a partner moved to State A before the complaint was filed, the partnership is a State A citizen*—just like the corporation. Therefore, the parties are not diverse and the partnership's motion to dismiss should be granted (Choice D).

*The partnership is also a citizen of any other state where other partners are domiciled.

(Choice B) Most defenses are waived if they are not asserted in a defendant's answer. But a defense based on lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is never waived and can be asserted by a party or raised by the court at any time.

(Choice C) Although neither of the company's claims independently exceeds $75,000, the company can aggregate (ie, combine) them to $90,000 to satisfy the amount-in-controversy requirement for diversity jurisdiction.

📌 Educational Objective

For purposes of diversity jurisdiction, a corporation is a citizen of every state where it is incorporated and/or has its principal place of business. An unincorporated association is a citizen of every state where its members are domiciled—ie, where the members reside and intend to remain indefinitely.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).
  • Carden v. Arkoma Assocs., 494 U.S. 185, 195–96 (1990) (holding that an unincorporated association, such as a partnership, is a citizen of every state where its members are domiciled).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Diversity jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：有限合伙/合伙的 公民身份（citizenship） 怎么算，导致 多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction） 成不成立。

三秒认题路径：

公司看注册地 → 合伙看成员住所 → 有无同州 → 不同州才行 → 本题不多元

核心法律规则

公司（corporation） 是它 注册地（state of incorporation） 和 主要营业地（principal place of business） 的公民，所以这家公司是 State A 公民。合伙（partnership） 属于 非公司组织（unincorporated association），考场意思：要看每个合伙人的 住所地（domicile）。

题干说有一个合伙人在起诉前已经搬到 State A，所以合伙也是 State A 公民。双方同州，完全多元（complete diversity） 没了，联邦法院就不能靠 diversity 管这个案子。

核心判例： Carden v. Arkoma Assocs. — 非公司组织按成员住所算公民身份，所以合伙人搬到 State A 会把合伙“拉成”State A 公民。

思维导图

公司 注册地/主要营业地 = State A
⇄
合伙 看每个成员 domicile
→
关键合伙人 起诉前已迁入 State A
→
结果 双方同州，不多元
起诉时双方是否为不同州公民？
否： 合伙成员里有人已是 State A 住所地公民，和公司重合。
卡死点：不是看“合伙总部在哪”，而是看成员 domicile。
结论： diversity 不成立，选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司在 State A，合伙在 State B，看起来像是 不同州，所以应该有管辖权。

但考试真正问的是：合伙不是按“名字”算公民，而是按 成员住所 算；题干已经告诉你有成员在起诉前迁到 State A，直接把多元管辖打掉了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的公司外壳看起来在哪个州」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 合伙成员在起诉前已迁入 State A，合伙因此也是 State A 公民；公司同州，完全多元（complete diversity） 失败。

❌ 概念混淆 | 组织类型误判

✕ A: 把合伙当公司看了，错把 diverse 直接套上去。

❌ 法律适用 | 主张放弃误判

✕ B: subject-matter jurisdiction 这张牌不会因没写进答辩就消失。

❌ 事实误判 | 金额拆分偷换

✕ C: 盯着单个请求金额不够，忘了这里先卡在 diversity 本身。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看主体身份，再算公民身份；先过多元，再碰金额，程序顺序不要反。

考场速记

记忆口诀：公司看注册地 + 主要营业地；合伙看成员 domicile。一旦成员里有人和对方同州，先别管钱够不够，完全多元（complete diversity） 已经没了。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A popular food blogger from State A got into a heated online argument with the owner of a successful vegan restaurant located in State B about the merits of veganism. To get back at the owner, the blogger wrote a review of the owner's vegan restaurant in which she falsely claimed that the restaurant was infested with vermin and used animal products in its cuisine. The blogger had never eaten at the owner's restaurant or traveled to State B. The blog post had over 500,000 views from people around the United States. Within one month of the post, the restaurant shut down.
The owner sued the blogger in a federal court in State B for defamation. Based on the allegations in the owner's complaint, the blogger filed a motion to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.
State B has a long-arm statute that gives its courts personal jurisdiction over out-of-state defendants that intentionally harm State B residents or businesses.
How will the federal court likely rule on the blogger's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the blogger knew that her review would negatively impact the restaurant in State B.
choices.B: Deny the motion, unless the blogger failed to attach an affidavit to the motion demonstrating why personal jurisdiction does not exist.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the blogger has never traveled to State B.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the blogger wrote the review in State A.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Requirements for specific jurisdiction
Long-arm
statute		 Forum state statute must authorize jurisdiction under specific circumstances
Due
process		 Minimum
contacts		 Purposeful availment of forum state's laws so suit is foreseeable:
  • Stream of commerce test – defendant places goods in stream of commerce & takes action that intentionally targets forum state
  • Effects test – defendant commits intentional tort in one state with intent that effects will be felt in forum state
Fair play &
substantial
justice		 Reasonableness factors:
  • Burden on defendant to appear & defend in forum state
  • Plaintiff's interest in obtaining relief in forum state
  • Forum state's interest
  • Interstate judicial system's interest in obtaining most efficient resolution of disputes
  • Interest of several states in furthering fundamental substantive social policies

A federal court* has specific personal jurisdiction over a nonresident defendant if (1) the forum state has a long-arm statute that authorizes jurisdiction under the specific circumstances and (2) applying that statute complies with due process. This due process requirement is met when:

  • the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and
  • the exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

Minimum contacts exist when the defendant purposefully avails him/herself of the state's protections and benefits so that the defendant should reasonably foresee being sued there. Purposeful availment can occur even if the defendant never physically enters the forum state—eg, committing an intentional tort in one state with the intent that the effects will be felt in the forum state ((Choices C & D)).

(Choice A) Here, State B's long-arm statute authorizes jurisdiction over out-of-state defendants (the blogger) who intentionally harm a State B business or resident (the owner). Applying the statute complies with due process because the blogger purposefully availed herself of State B's benefits when she wrote a review to harm the owner in State B—making this defamation suit foreseeable there. And since there is no indication that exercising jurisdiction would offend notions of fair play and substantial justice, the State B federal court has specific jurisdiction over the blogger. Therefore, her motion to dismiss will likely be denied.

*Federal courts have the same jurisdictional reach as courts of the state in which they sit.

(Choice B) When a defendant asserts lack of personal jurisdiction in a pre-answer motion to dismiss (as seen here), the defendant can use the allegations in the pleadings or an attached affidavit to show why personal jurisdiction does not exist.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant has minimum contacts with a forum state when he/she purposefully avails him/herself of the state's protections and benefits, so that a lawsuit is reasonably foreseeable there. This can occur when the defendant commits an intentional tort in one state with the purpose or knowledge that the effects will be felt in the forum state.

📚 References
  • Calder v. Jones, 465 U.S. 783, 789–90 (1984) (holding that out-of-state defendants were subject to specific jurisdiction because their libelous article intentionally targeted the forum state's resident).
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the minimum contacts required for specific jurisdiction).

zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，除非博主未能随动议附上宣誓书 (affidavit) 以证明为何不存在人身管辖权。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为博主从未去过B州。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction and Venue - Personal jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州外博主写诽谤帖子，是否因为明知伤害会落到州内商家，就能构成 特定管辖（specific personal jurisdiction）。

三秒认题路径：

长臂法 → 最低联系 → 效果落州内 → 公平正义 → 可管辖

核心法律规则

只抓本题够用的规则

联邦法院的 特定人身管辖（specific personal jurisdiction） 先看州的 长臂法（long-arm statute），再看是否符合正当程序。

正当程序要求被告有 最低联系（minimum contacts），也就是被告主动把自己和本州连起来，让“会被本州起诉”变得可预见。

对 故意侵权（intentional tort），如果被告在州外下手，但明知后果会在论坛州出现，这就是 effects test；考试意思：你没进州，也可能被州内起诉。

核心判例： Calder v. Jones —— 故意把诽谤指向论坛州居民，足以支持特定管辖。

思维导图

州 B 长臂法是否授权？
是：故意伤害州 B 商家/居民 → 法律先放行。
正当程序是否满足？
最低联系：州外发帖，但目标是州 B 的餐馆，且她知道后果会落在州 B。
effects test：诽谤在州 A 写出，但她就是冲着州 B 的影响去的。
公平正义：题干没给出明显负担过重或不公，通常不推翻管辖。
结论
答案：州 B 联邦法院可以管辖 → 驳回撤诉。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她人没去过州 B，帖子也是在州 A 写的，所以州 B 不能管。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有故意把伤害打到州 B，让诉讼在州 B 可预见（foreseeable）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 knowingly hurt the State B restaurant 正好对应 effects test；她明知影响会落在州 B，所以驳回撤诉。

❌ 法律适用 | 撤诉材料误判

✕ B: 把 affidavit 当成决定管辖的门槛了。

❌ 事实误判 | 旅行细节偷换

✕ C: 抓住 never traveled 就下结论，忽略了故意指向州内的效果。

❌ 概念混淆 | 地点因素误读

✕ D: 以为 wrote the review 在州 A 就一定只算州 A 的联系。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看长臂法，再盯住故意侵权的效果落点；只要目标瞄准论坛州，物理没进州也可能有管辖。

考场速记

记住一句：“打向州内的故意侵权，最容易成立特定管辖。” 看到州外发帖、州内受害，就先想 Calder。

口诀：故意打中州内 → 你就可能被州内告。
